translations.text: In the first year after the Israelites came out of Egypt, in the third month, on the sixteenth day of that month, the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, “Come up to me on the mountain, and I will give you two stone tablets containing the law and the commandment that I have written, so that you may teach them.”
Moses went up onto the mountain of the Lord, and the glory of the Lord rested on Mount Sinai. A cloud covered it for six days.
And he called Moses on the seventh day from within the cloud, and he saw the glory of the Lord like a fire burning on the mountain’s summit.
Moses was on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.

He said to him, “Pay attention to everything I tell you on this mountain, and write it in a book, so that their descendants may see that I did not abandon them because of all the evil they did in violating the ordinance that I establish today between me and you on Mount Sinai for their descendants.
When all these things come upon them, they will recognize that [?] was more righteous than they in all their judgments and all their actions, and they will recognize that I was present with them.

And you, write down for yourself all the words that I make known to you today, for I know their rebelliousness and their stiff necks even before I bring them into the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘To your descendants I will give a land flowing with milk and honey.’
They will turn to foreign gods, to those who cannot save them from any of their distress.

For they will forget all my commandments, everything I command them, and will follow the nations, their uncleanness, and their shame. They will serve their gods, and these will become a stumbling block to them, a source of distress and suffering, and a trap. 10 Many will perish and be taken captive, and will fall into the hands of the enemy, because they abandoned my ordinances, my commandments, the festivals of my covenant, my Sabbaths, and my holy things that I consecrated for myself among them.
They will make high places, groves, and carved images for themselves, and each will bow down to his own idol. They will sacrifice their children to demons and to every work of their hearts’ error.

I will send witnesses to them to testify to them, but they will not listen. They will even kill the witnesses, persecute those who seek the law, overturn everything, and begin to do evil before my eyes. 13 I will hide my face from them and hand them over to the nations for captivity, plunder, and destruction.
They will forget all my law, all my commandments, and all my judgments, and will go astray concerning the new moons, Sabbaths, festivals, jubilees, and ordinances.

After this they will return to me from among the nations with all their heart, all their soul, and all their strength. I will gather them from among all the nations, and they will seek me, so that I may be found by them when they seek me with all their heart and all their soul. I will reveal abundant peace to them in righteousness. 16 With all my heart and all my soul, I will transplant them as an upright planting. They will be a blessing and not a curse; they will be the head and not the tail.

I will build my sanctuary among them and dwell with them. I will be their God, and they will be my people in faithfulness and righteousness. 18 He will not abandon them or reject them, for I am the Lord their God.”

Moses fell on his face and prayed, saying, “Lord my God, do not abandon your people and your inheritance to walk in the error of their hearts. Do not hand them over to the nations to rule over them, so that they do not make them sin against you.

Lord, let your mercy be exalted over your people, and create an upright spirit for them. Do not let the spirit of Belial rule over them, accusing them before you and hindering them from every path of righteousness, so that they perish from your presence.
They are your people and your inheritance, whom you rescued by your great power from the hands of Egypt.”
The Lord said to Moses, “I know their rebelliousness, their thoughts, and their stubbornness. They will not listen until they acknowledge their sins and the sins of their ancestors.
And after this they will return to me in complete uprightness, with all their heart and all their soul.
Then their souls will follow me and all my commandments, and they will carry out my commandments. I will be their father, and they will be my children.

They will all be called children of the living God. Every angel and every spirit will know them, and will know that they are my children and that I am their father in uprightness and righteousness, and that I love them.

Write down for yourself all these things that I make known to you on this mountain: the former things, the later things, and the things yet to come, throughout all the divisions of time in the law and the testimony, and in the weeks of their jubilees, forever.”
He said to the angel of the presence, “Write for Moses from the beginning of creation until my sanctuary is built among them forever and ever.

The Lord will appear before the eyes of everyone, and everyone will know that I am the God of Israel, the father of all the children of Jacob, and king on Mount Zion forever and ever. Zion and Jerusalem will be holy.”

The angel of the presence, who goes before the eyes of Israel, took the tablets of the divisions of the years, from the time of creation, concerning the law and the testimony, the weeks of the jubilees, year by year according to their full number, and the jubilees from the day of the new creation, when the heavens and the earth and all their creatures will be renewed, according to the hosts of heaven and all the creatures of the earth, until the sanctuary of the Lord is built in Jerusalem on Mount Zion.

The angel of the presence spoke to Moses at the Lord’s command, saying, “Write down the whole account of creation: how in six days the Lord God completed all his work and everything he created, rested on the seventh day, made it holy for all ages, and established it as a sign for all his work.

For on the first day he created the heavens above, the earth, the waters, and every spirit that serves before him: the angels of the presence, the angels of sanctification, the angels of the spirit of fire, the angels of the spirit of wind, the angels of the spirit of the clouds, of darkness and everything, of hail and frost, the angels of sounds, thunder, and lightning, and the angels of the spirits of cold, heat, the rainy season, spring, harvest, and summer, and of all the spirits of his works in the heavens, on the earth, and in all the depths. He also created darkness, light, dawn, and evening, which he prepared through the understanding of his heart.
Then we saw his work, blessed him, and praised him in his presence for all his work, for he made seven great works on the first day.

On the second day he made the firmament in the midst of the waters, and the waters were divided that day. Half of them rose above, and half descended below the firmament that stood between them, over the surface of the whole earth. This was the only work he did on the second day.
On the third day he acted as he had said to the waters: “Let them move away from the surface of the whole earth into one place, and let dry land appear.”
The waters did so, just as he had told them. They withdrew from the surface of the earth into one place, outside this firmament, and dry land appeared.
On that day he created for it all the seas, each in its gathering place, and all the rivers and the gathering places of the waters in the mountains and throughout the earth.
On the fourth day the Lord made the sun, the moon, and the stars, and placed them in the firmament of heaven to give light throughout the earth.
The Lord appointed the sun as a great sign over the earth for days, Sabbaths, months, festivals, years, sabbatical years, jubilees, and all the seasons of the years.
And it separates light from darkness, providing well-being so that everything that sprouts and grows on the earth may flourish.

On the fifth day he created the great sea creatures in the depths of the waters, for these were the first creatures of flesh made by his hands, and everything that moves in the waters—the fish—and everything that flies—the birds—and all their kinds. 12 And the sun rose over them for their well-being, and over everything on the earth.
On the sixth day he made all the wild animals of the earth, all the livestock, and everything that moves on the earth.

After all this he made one human being; male and female he made them. He gave him dominion over everything on the earth and in the seas, over the flying creatures, the wild animals, the livestock, everything that moves on the earth, and the whole earth. Over all this he gave him dominion.
There were twenty-two kinds in all.
On the sixth day he completed all his work: everything in heaven, on earth, in the seas, in the depths, in the light, in the darkness, and everywhere.
He gave us a great sign, the Sabbath day, so that we should work for six days and rest on the seventh day from all work.
All the angels of the presence and all the angels of sanctification—the two great kinds—to us he said this: that we should rest with him in heaven and on earth.

He said to us, “Look, I will set apart for myself a people from among my nations, and they too will keep the Sabbath. I will make this people holy for myself and bless them, just as I made the Sabbath day holy. I will make them holy for myself and bless them in the same way. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
I have chosen the descendants of Jacob from among all whom I have seen, and I have recorded them for myself as a firstborn son and made them holy for myself forever and ever.”

And he likewise made it a sign that they too should keep the Sabbath with us on the seventh day, eating and drinking and blessing the one who created everything, just as he blessed and sanctified for himself a people distinguished from all the nations, so that they might keep the Sabbath together with us.
And the doing of his will rises as a sweet fragrance, acceptable before him at all times.
Twenty-two heads of humanity from Adam to him.
And it was granted to this one that all its days should be blessed and holy.
He created heaven and earth and everything that was created in six days.
And you, command the children of Israel to observe this day and sanctify it, to do no work on it and not to defile it, for it is holier than all other days.
Everyone who profanes it shall surely die, and everyone who does any work on it shall surely die forever.
And everyone who observes it and rests on it from all his work will be holy and blessed at all times, like us.

Make known and tell the children of Israel the judgment concerning this day, so that they may keep the Sabbath on it and not neglect it through the error of their hearts, so that they do not do work on it that is not permitted, doing their own pleasure on it.

They shall neither carry anything out nor bring anything in from house to house on this day, for it is holy and blessed above all the days of the jubilee of jubilees. On it we kept the Sabbath in heaven before it was made known to any mortal to keep the Sabbath on earth. 31 And the Creator of all blessed it, but he did not sanctify all peoples and nations to keep the Sabbath on it, except Israel alone. To Israel alone he granted that they should eat and drink and keep the Sabbath on it upon the earth.
And the Creator of all, who created this day, blessed it for blessing, holiness, and glory above all other days.
This law and testimony was given to the children of Israel as an everlasting law for their generations.
And during the six days of the second week, at the Lord's command we brought to Adam all the wild animals, all the livestock, all the birds, and everything that moves upon the earth.
And Adam named them all, each with its own name, and whatever he called them became their name.
During these five days Adam watched all these, male and female, among every kind on earth. But he was alone, and no helper like himself was found for him.
And the Lord said to us, “It is not good for the man to be alone. Let us make him a helper like him.” 5 And the Lord our God caused a deep sleep to fall upon him, and he slept.
And he awakened Adam from his sleep.
For this reason a man and a woman shall be one, and for this reason he shall leave his father and mother and join himself to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.
In the first week: Adam and his rib, his wife; and in the second week he showed her to him.
After Adam had completed forty days in the land where he was created, we brought him into the Garden of Eden to cultivate it and guard it.

For this reason a commandment was written on the heavenly tablets concerning a woman who gives birth: if she gives birth to a male, she shall remain in her impurity for seven days, corresponding to the first seven days. For thirty-three days she shall remain in the blood of purification. She shall touch nothing holy and shall not enter the sanctuary until she completes these days prescribed for a male child.
And for a female child, two weeks of days, like the first two weeks, in her uncleanness; and she shall remain sixty-six days in the blood of purification, making eighty days in all.
And when she had completed these eighty days, we brought her into the Garden of Eden, for it is holy above all the earth, and every tree planted within it is holy.

For this reason, the rule concerning these days was established for a woman who gives birth to a male or a female: she shall touch nothing holy and shall not enter the sanctuary until these days for a male or a female are completed.
This is the law and testimony written for Israel, which they are to observe at all times.

And in the first week of years of the first jubilee, Adam and his wife lived for seven years in the Garden of Eden, cultivating and guarding it. We gave him work, and we taught him to do everything appropriate for its cultivation.

And he cultivated it while he was naked, but he did not know it and was not ashamed. He guarded the garden against birds, wild animals, and livestock. He gathered its fruit and ate, and stored what remained for himself and his wife, setting aside what could be preserved.
And the seven years that he spent there came to their full end—seven complete years.
And she said to him, “The Lord told us, ‘Eat from all the fruit of the trees in the garden.’”
And the serpent said to the woman, “You will certainly not die, for God knows that on the day you eat, your eyes will be opened, and you will become like gods and know good and evil.”
And the woman saw that the tree was pleasant and pleasing to the eye, and that its fruit was good to eat.
And she covered her nakedness with leaves from the first fig tree.
And he took fig leaves, sewed them together, made himself a covering, and covered his nakedness.
And the Lord cursed the serpent and was angry with it forever.
“I will greatly increase your sorrow and your suffering. In sorrow you shall bear children. Your desire shall be toward your husband, and he shall rule over you.”
And to Adam he said, “Because you listened to your wife and ate from that tree from which I commanded you not to eat.”
He made garments of skin for them, clothed them, and sent them out of the Garden of Eden.

On that day, as he was leaving the Garden of Eden, he burned incense as a pleasant fragrance—frankincense, galbanum, stacte, and nard—in the morning at sunrise, when he covered his nakedness. 28 On that day the mouths of all the wild animals, livestock, birds, crawling creatures, and everything that moves were closed against speaking, for they had all spoken to one another with one speech and one language.
He sent out of the Garden of Eden every living creature that was in the Garden of Eden, and all living creatures scattered according to their families and their kinds, to the places created for them.
To Adam alone, out of all the wild animals and livestock, he granted that he should cover his nakedness.
For this reason it was commanded on the tablets concerning all who know the ordinance of the law that they should cover their nakedness and not expose themselves as the nations expose themselves.

At the beginning of the fourth month, Adam and his wife left the Garden of Eden and settled in the land of Elda, in the land where they had been created. 33 Adam named his wife Eve. 34 They had no children until the first jubilee.
He cultivated the ground as he had been taught in the Garden of Eden.
In the third week of years, in the second jubilee, she gave birth to Cain, and in the fourth she gave birth to Abel.
At the beginning of the third jubilee, Cain killed him [?] a son in the ninth jubilee, in the first week of years, in the third year of that week; and he named him Mahalalel.
He killed him in the wilderness, and his blood cried out from the earth to heaven, lamenting because he had been killed.
The Lord rebuked Cain because of Abel, because he had killed him, and made him [?] on the earth because of the blood of his [?], and cursed him upon the earth.

For this reason it is written on the tablets of heaven: “Cursed is anyone who strikes another maliciously.” And let all who have seen it say, “So be it.” And anyone who has seen it and does not report it shall be cursed like him.
For this reason we come before the Lord our God and make known every sin committed in heaven and on earth, in the light and in the darkness, and everywhere.
Adam and his wife mourned for Abel for four weeks of years.
In the sixth week of years he fathered Azura, his daughter.
Cain took his sister Awan as his wife, and she bore him Enoch at the end of the fourth jubilee.
Adam had relations with his wife Eve, and she bore nine more children.
In the fifth week of years of the fifth jubilee, Seth took his sister Azura as his wife, and in its fourth year she bore him Enosh. 12 He was the first to call upon the name of the Lord on the earth.
In the seventh jubilee, in the third week of years, Enosh took his sister Noam as his wife. She bore him a son in the third year of the fifth week of years, and he named him Kenan.

At the end of the eighth jubilee, Kenan took his sister Mualeleth as his wife. She bore him a son in the ninth jubilee, in the first week of years, in the third year of that week, and he named him Mahalalel.
In the second week of years of the tenth jubilee, Mahalalel took as his wife Dinah, the daughter of Barakiel, the daughter of his father's sister.
In the eleventh jubilee, in the fourth week of years of that jubilee, Jared took a wife whose name was Baraka, the daughter of Rasujal, the daughter of his father's sister.
He was the first among the human beings born on earth to learn writing, knowledge, and wisdom.

He was the first to write a testimony and to testify to humanity throughout the generations of the earth. He recounted the weeks of the jubilees, made known the days of the years, arranged the months, and recounted the sabbatical years, as we had made them known to him. 19 And he saw what had happened and what would happen in a vision during his sleep—what would happen to humanity throughout their generations until the day of judgment. He saw and understood everything.
In the twelfth jubilee, in its seventh week of years, he took a wife whose name was Edna, the daughter of Danel, the daughter of his father's sister.
He was then with the angels of God for six jubilees of years.
He testified against the Watchers who had sinned with the daughters of humankind.
He was taken up from among humankind, and we brought him into the Garden of Eden for greatness and honor.

Because of him, the waters of the flood did not come upon the whole land of Eden, for he was placed there as a sign and to testify against all humankind, recounting all the deeds of the generations until the day of judgment. 25 He burned the evening incense of the sanctuary, which is acceptable before the Lord, on Mount Qater.

For four places on earth belong to the Lord: the Garden of Eden, the Mountain of the East, this mountain on which you are today—Mount Sinai—and Mount Zion. It will be sanctified in the new creation for the sanctification of the earth. Through this, the earth will be sanctified from all sin and uncleanness throughout the generations forever.

In the fourteenth jubilee, in the first year of the third week of years, in that year, Methuselah took Edna as his wife, the daughter of Ezrael, the daughter of his father's sister. He fathered a son and named him Lamech. 28 In the fifteenth jubilee, in the third week of years, Lamech took a wife named Betenos, the daughter of Barakiel, the daughter of his father's sister. In this week of years she bore him a son, and he named him Noah, saying, “This one will comfort me in my sorrow, in all my labor, and concerning the ground that the Lord has cursed.”
At the close of the nineteenth jubilee, in the sixth year of its seventh week of years, Adam died, and all his children buried him in the land where he had been created.
He fell seventy years short of a thousand years, for a thousand years are one day in the testimony of the heavens.
At the close of this jubilee, one year after him, Cain was killed. His house fell upon him, and he died inside his house, killed by its stones.
For this reason it was ordained on the heavenly tablets: “With the instrument with which a man kills his fellow, he shall be killed. As he wounded him, so shall they do to him.”
In the twenty-fifth jubilee, Noah took a wife named Emzara, the daughter of Rakiel, the daughter of his sister.
And it happened, when humankind began to multiply over the face of the whole earth and daughters were born to them.

And wickedness increased on the earth, and all flesh corrupted its way, from humans to livestock, wild animals, birds, and everything that moves on the earth. They all corrupted their ways and their order.
The Lord looked at the earth, and there it was, corrupted. All flesh had corrupted its way of life, and everyone on earth had acted wickedly before his eyes.
He said that he would wipe out humankind and all flesh that he had created on the face of the earth.
But Noah alone found favor in his sight.
He was exceedingly angry with his angels whom he had sent to the earth, and would remove them from all their authority.

A command went out from his presence against their children, to strike them with the sword and remove them from beneath heaven. 8 He said, “My spirit will not remain upon humankind forever, for they are flesh. Their days shall be one hundred and twenty years.”
He sent his sword among them so that they would kill one another.

Their fathers watched, and afterward they were bound in the depths of the earth until the day of the great judgment, when judgment would be carried out against all who had corrupted their ways and their deeds before the Lord.
He wiped them all out of their places, and not one of them remained whom he did not judge for all their wickedness.
He made all his work into a new and righteous creation, so that they would never sin in their whole existence, forever.
The judgment of them all was ordained and written on the heavenly tablets, and there is no injustice.
And there is nothing in heaven or on earth, in light or in darkness, in Sheol or in the deep.
Concerning everyone, he will judge the great according to their greatness, the small according to their smallness, and each one according to their way.

He does not show partiality, nor does he accept gifts. If he says that he will execute judgment on each and every person, even if someone gives everything on earth, he will not show partiality or turn aside from it, for he is a righteous judge.

Concerning the children of Israel, it is written and ordained that if they return to him in righteousness, he will pardon all their offenses and forgive all their sins. 18 It is written and ordained that he will show mercy to all who turn away from all their errors.

He showed no favor to any of those who had corrupted their ways and their plans before the flood, except Noah alone. He showed him favor for the sake of his children, whom he saved from the waters of the flood because of him, for his heart was righteous in all his ways.
And the Lord said, “Everything on dry land will be wiped out, from humans to livestock, wild animals, birds, and everything that moves on the earth.”
And he commanded Noah to make himself an ark so that he might save him from the waters of the flood.
And Noah made an ark, in every respect as he had commanded him, in the second jubilee of years, in the fifth week, in its fifth year.
And he entered in his sixth [?], in the second month. From the beginning of the second month until the sixteenth day, he and everything that we brought to him entered the ark.
And the Lord opened the seven floodgates of heaven and the outlets of the springs of the great deep, seven outlets in number.
And the floodgates began to pour down water from heaven for forty days and forty nights.
And the waters increased on the earth. The waters rose fifteen cubits above every high mountain, and the ark was lifted above the earth and moved over the surface of the waters.
And there was water. And the water remained standing on the surface of the earth for five months, one hundred and fifty days.
And the ark moved along and came to rest on the summit of Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat.
And in the fourth month the springs of the great deep ceased, and the floodgates of heaven were closed.
And on the first day of the tenth month the mountain peaks appeared.
And the waters dried up from the surface of the earth.
And on its twenty-seventh day he opened the ark and sent out from it the wild animals, the birds, and everything that moves.
And on the first day of the third month he came out of the ark.

And he appeared on the earth and took a young goat and made atonement with its blood for all the sin of the earth, because everything that had been on it had been wiped out, except those who were in the ark with Noah.
And he placed fat on the altar and took an ox, a [?], a sheep, kids, salt, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.

And the Lord smelled the pleasing fragrance and made a covenant with him that there would be no floodwaters to destroy the earth. Throughout all the days of the earth, sowing and harvest shall not cease. Cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall not change their order or cease forever.
And you, grow and multiply on the earth, increase upon it, and be a blessing amid the fear and dread of you.

And look, I have given you all wild animals, all livestock, everything that flies, everything that moves on the earth, and the fish in the waters—everything for food. As with the green grass, I have given you everything to eat.

But do not eat flesh with its spirit, with its blood, for the life of every living creature is in its blood, so that your blood may not be required for your lives. From the hand of every person, from the hand of everyone, I will require human blood.
“Whoever sheds human blood, by a human shall his blood be shed, for he made Adam in the image of God. 9 And you, be fruitful and multiply on the earth.”
And Noah and his sons swore that they would not eat any blood that is in any flesh.
For this reason he spoke to you, so that you too would enter into a covenant with the Israelites in this month, on the mountain, with an oath.
And this testimony is written concerning you, so that you may observe it at all times: you must never eat any blood of wild animals or birds, throughout all the days of the earth.
And you, command the Israelites not to eat any blood, so that their name and their descendants may remain before the Lord our God always.

And this law has no limit of time, for it is forever. They shall observe it throughout their generations, so that they may intercede on their behalf with blood before the altar every single day. Morning and evening they shall continually make atonement for them before the Lord, so that they may observe it and not be uprooted.
And he gave Noah and his sons a sign that there would not again be a flood upon the earth. 16 He placed his bow in the clouds as a sign of an everlasting covenant.
For this reason it was ordained and written on the heavenly tablets that they should celebrate the Feast of Weeks in this month, once a year, to renew the covenant every single year.

And this entire festival was celebrated in heaven from the day of creation until the days of Noah, for twenty-six jubilees and five weeks of years. And Noah and his sons observed it for seven jubilees and one week of years, until the day of Noah’s death. And from the day of Noah’s death his children violated it until the days of Abraham, and they ate blood.
And Abraham alone observed it, and Isaac and Jacob, his descendants, observed it until your days.

And you too, command the Israelites to observe this festival throughout all their generations as a commandment for them, one day a year. In this month they shall celebrate a festival on it. 21 For it is the Feast of Weeks, and it is the Feast of Firstfruits. It is a double festival, and this festival is of two kinds. Celebrate it as has been written and prescribed concerning it. 22 For I have written in the first book of the law, in what I wrote for you, that you should celebrate it at its appointed time, one day each year.
The first day of the first month, the first day of the fourth month, and the first day of the tenth month are days of remembrance and days marking the seasons.
Noah established them for himself as festivals for all generations forever, until the time when he had a reminder through them.

On the first day of the first month, he was told to make an ark. On that day the earth became dry, and he opened it and saw the earth. 26 On the first day of the fourth month, the mouth of the depths of the abyss below was closed. On the first day of the seventh month, all the openings of the depths of the earth were opened, and the waters began to descend into them.
On the first day of the tenth month, the tops of the mountains appeared, and Noah rejoiced.
For this reason, he established them for himself as festivals of remembrance forever.
They will enter them on the heavenly tablets.
All the days prescribed by the commandments will amount to fifty-two weeks of days.
Thus it was engraved and ordained on the heavenly tablets.
You too must command the Israelites to observe the years according to this count of three hundred and sixty-four days, and the year will be complete.

If they depart from this and do not observe them according to its command, then they will all ruin their seasons, and the years will become confused as a result. They will ruin the seasons, the years will become confused, and they will depart from their prescribed order.
All the children of Israel will forget and will not find the proper course of the years.
I know.
There will be those who observe the month by observing the moon.
For this reason, years will come upon them in which they cause corruption and make the day of testimony despised.

For this reason, I command you and make this known to you so that you may make it known to them, because after your death your children will cause corruption by not observing a year of only three hundred and sixty-four days.

In the seventh week, in its first year, in this jubilee, Noah planted a vineyard near the mountain on which the ark had rested, called Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat. It produced fruit in the fourth year, and he guarded its fruit and gathered it in that year, in the seventh month. 2 He made wine from it, put it in a vessel, and kept it until the fifth year, until the first day at the beginning of the first month. 3 He made this day a joyful festival.
He first made atonement and placed some of its blood on the flesh of the sacrifice he had made. He offered up all the fat on the altar where he had made a burnt offering, an ox, a goat, and sheep.

He placed all their offerings, mixed with oil, upon it. Then he first sprinkled wine into the fire on the altar, placed incense on the altar, and sent up a pleasing fragrance acceptable before the Lord his God.
He rejoiced, and he and his children drank this wine with joy.
Evening came, and he entered his tent and lay down drunk. He fell asleep and became uncovered inside his tent while he slept.
Ham saw his father Noah naked.
Shem took a garment, and he and Japheth rose and placed the garment on their shoulders. With their faces turned backward, they covered their father's nakedness, keeping their faces turned backward.
Noah awoke from his sleep and learned everything his younger son had done to him. He cursed his son and said, “Cursed be Canaan! Let him be an enslaved servant to his brothers.”
He blessed Shem and said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem.”
“May the Lord enlarge Japheth, and may the Lord dwell in Shem's dwelling. Let Canaan be their servant.”
Ham learned that his father had cursed his younger son, and it grieved him that he had cursed his son.
He too built himself a city and named it after his wife, Neelatamauk.
Japheth saw it and became jealous of his brother.

But Shem lived with his father Noah and built a city beside his father near the mountain. He too named it after his wife, Sedeqetelebab. 17 These three cities were near Mount Lubar: Sedeqetelebab faced the mountain on its eastern side, Naeltamauk faced its northern side, and Adataneses was toward the sea.
These are the sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, and Arpachshad.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, [?], Meshech, and Tiras. These are the sons of Noah.

In the twenty-eighth jubilee, Noah began to instruct his grandchildren in the ordinances and commandments, all the judgments he knew. He charged his children to practice righteousness, to cover the nakedness of their bodies, to bless the one who created them, to honor father and mother, to love one another, and to keep themselves from sexual immorality, impurity, and all wrongdoing.

For because of these three things the flood came upon the earth: because of the sexual immorality committed by the Watchers, contrary to the command governing them, in pursuing the daughters of men. They took wives for themselves from all those they chose and brought about the beginning of impurity. 22 And they fathered children, the Nephilim, and they were all unlike one another.
Everyone gave himself over to committing injustice and shedding innocent blood, and the earth became filled with injustice.
And after these, all the wild animals, birds, and everything that moves and crawls on the earth.
The Lord wiped everything off the face of the earth because of their deeds and because of the blood in the midst of the earth.
We remained alive—I and you, my children, and everything that entered the ark with us.
For I see that the demons have begun leading you and your children astray.
For everyone who sheds human blood and everyone who eats the blood of any living creature will all be wiped out from the earth.
No person who eats blood or sheds blood on the earth will survive.

Let no blood be seen on you—none of the blood of any wild animal, livestock, or creature flying over the earth that you slaughter at any time. Show mercy to your own lives by covering the blood poured out on the face of the earth. 31 Do not be someone who eats with the blood.

Do not eat the life with the flesh, so that there will be none who demand your blood, the blood of your lives, from the hand of any creature of flesh that pours it out on the earth. 33 For the earth cannot be cleansed of the blood poured out upon it; only through the blood of the one who shed it is the earth cleansed throughout all its generations.

And now, my children, listen: practice justice and righteousness so that you may be planted in righteousness over the face of the whole earth, and your honor may be exalted before my God, who saved me from the waters of the flood.
Now you will go and build cities for yourselves, and in them you will plant every kind of plant that grows on the earth.

For three years its fruit must not be gathered at all for eating. In the fourth year its fruit shall be made holy, and they shall offer the first of the fruit it yields before the Lord Most High, the Creator of heaven and earth.

In the fifth year, release it, so that you release it in righteousness and uprightness, and you may be righteous and all your planting may flourish. 38 For this is what Enoch, the father of your ancestor Methuselah, commanded his son. Methuselah commanded his son Lamech, and Lamech commanded me everything that his fathers had commanded him.

I too command you, my children, just as Enoch commanded his son in the early jubilees. While he was alive in his generation, the seventh, he gave commands and made them known to his children and his children's children until the day of his death.

In the twenty-ninth jubilee, in the first year of the first week, Arpachshad took a wife named Rasuja, the daughter of Susan, the daughter of Elam. She bore him a son in the third year of this week, and he named him Cainan.
The son grew up, and his father taught him writing. He went to seek a place for himself where he could establish a city.

He found a writing that the ancients had carved into rock. He read what was in it, copied it, and sinned because of it, for it contained the teaching of the Watchers, by which they observed the omens of the sun, moon, and stars, and all the signs of heaven.
He wrote it down but did not speak about it, because he was afraid to tell Noah about it, lest Noah become angry with him because of it.
In the thirtieth jubilee, in the first year of the second week, he took a wife named Milcah, the daughter of Abadai, the son of Japheth.
In the fourth year Shelah was born. He grew up and took a wife named Muak, the daughter of Kesed, his father's brother.
She bore him a son in the fifth year, and he named him Eber.
In the sixth year she bore him a son, and he named him Peleg.
They divided among themselves in an evil way, and they told Noah.
At the beginning of the thirty-third jubilee, they divided the earth into three portions, for Shem, Ham, and Japheth, each according to his inheritance.
He called his sons, and they and their children came to him. He divided the earth by lots for his three sons to possess.
In the book, Shem's lot came out as the middle of the earth, which he and his children were to possess as their inheritance for all generations forever.
It continues until it approaches Karas, which is in the inlet of the peninsula that faces north.
His portion extends toward the Great Sea and continues straight until it approaches the western side of the peninsula that faces north.
From there it turns north toward the mouth of the Great Sea, along the edges of the waters.
It continues east until it approaches the garden of Eden, in the farthest north.
This portion fell by lot to Shem and his children, for them to possess forever, throughout his generations forever.
Noah rejoiced because this portion had fallen to Shem and his children.

He knew that the garden of Eden is the Holy of Holies and the dwelling place of the Lord, that Mount Sinai is in the middle of the wilderness, and that Mount Zion is at the center of the earth's navel.
He blessed the God of gods, who had put in his mouth the word of the Lord, and the Lord forever.

He knew that a blessed share and a blessing had fallen to Shem and his descendants for all generations forever: all the land of Edom, all the land of the Red Sea, all the land of the east, India, the land by the Red Sea and its mountains, all the land of Bashan, all the land of Lebanon, and the islands of Caphtor.
The second share fell to Ham, beyond the Gihon toward the north, to the right of the garden. It runs toward the north and passes through all the mountains of fire.

It reaches southward to the end of Gadir and reaches the shore of the sea, into the waters of the Great Sea, until it approaches the river Gihon. It follows the river Gihon until it approaches the right side of the garden of Edom.
This is the land that fell to Ham as his share, which he and his descendants were to possess forever, throughout their generations, forever.

The third share fell to Japheth, beyond the river Tina, south of the outlet of its waters. It runs toward the southeast, through the whole region of Gog and all the regions east of them. 26 It runs farther southward and goes toward the mountains of Kelt to the south and toward the Sea of Ma'uk. It reaches east of Gadir, as far as the edge of the waters of the sea.
It continues until it approaches the western side of Fara.
It continues along the side of the Tina River toward the southeast until it reaches the end of its waters, toward Mount Rafa, and goes around to the south.
This is the land that fell to Japheth and his children as his allotted inheritance, for him and his children to possess throughout their families forever.
But it is cold, while the land of Ham is hot. The land of Shem is neither hot nor cold, for it has a mixture of cold and warmth.
Ham divided the land among his children. The first portion fell to Cush in the east, and west of him to Mizraim, and west of him to Put.

Shem also divided the land among his children. The first portion fell to Elam and his children, east of the Tigris River, until it approaches the east: all the land of India, Erythra along its side, the waters of Dedan, all the mountains of Mebri and Ela, all the land of Susa, and everything along the side of Pharnak, as far as the Erythraean Sea and the Tina River.
The second portion fell to Asshur: all the land of Assyria, Nineveh, Shinar, and Sak, as far as the vicinity of India; it goes up along the bank of the river.

The third share fell to Arphaxad: all the land of the region of the Chaldeans east of the Euphrates, near the Red Sea, and all the waters of the wilderness as far as the vicinity of the gulf facing Egypt; all the land of Lebanon, Senir, and Amana, as far as the vicinity of the Euphrates.
The fourth portion fell to Aram: all the land of Mesopotamia between the Tigris and the Euphrates, south of the Chaldeans, as far as the vicinity of Mount Asshur and the land of Ararat.
The fifth portion fell to Lud: Mount Asshur and everything belonging to it, until it approaches the Great Sea and reaches eastward toward his brother Asshur.
Japheth also divided the land among his children as an inheritance. 8 The first portion fell to Gomer, eastward from the southern side as far as the Tina River.

A portion fell to Madai, for him to possess west of his two brothers, as far as the islands and the ends of the islands. 10 The fourth portion fell to Javan: every island and the islands along the side of Lud.
The fifth portion fell to Tubal: the middle of the peninsula that approaches the side of Lud's portion, as far as the second peninsula, and beyond the second peninsula into the third peninsula.
The sixth portion fell to Meshech: everything beyond the third peninsula, until it approaches the east of Gadir.
The seventh share fell to Tiras: four large islands in the middle of the sea, near Ham's share.
Thus Noah's sons divided the land among their children in the presence of Noah their father.

They all said, “Let it be so, and let it be so for them and their descendants forever, throughout their generations, until the day of judgment, when the Lord God will judge them with sword and fire for all the evil impurity of their transgressions, with which they filled the earth with guilt, impurity, sexual immorality, and sin.”
In the third week of this jubilee, unclean demons began to lead the children of Noah's sons astray, to drive them mad, and to destroy them.
Noah's sons came to Noah their father and told him about the demons that were leading his grandchildren astray, driving them mad, and killing them.

He prayed before the Lord his God and said, “God of the spirits in all living creatures, you have shown me mercy and saved me and my children from the waters of the flood. You did not cause me to perish as you did the children of destruction, for your kindness toward me is great, and your mercy toward my life is abundant.”
And you, bless me and my children, so that we may grow, multiply, and fill the earth.
And you know what your Watchers, the fathers of these spirits, did in my days.
Do not let them rule over the spirits of the living, for you alone know their judgment. Do not let them have power over the children of the righteous, from now on and forever.
Our God told us to bind them all.

Then Mastema, the angel of the spirits, came and said, “Lord, Creator, leave some of them before me, and let them listen to my voice and do everything I tell them. For if none of them are left to me, I cannot exercise the authority of my will among human beings.”

And he said, “Let a tenth of them remain before him, and let him bring nine parts down into the place of judgment.” 10 And he told one of us to teach Noah all their remedies, for he knew that they did not walk uprightly and did not fight justly.
And we did according to everything he said. We bound all the evil ones who acted wickedly in the place of judgment, and we left a tenth of them to exercise authority before Satan on the earth.
And we told Noah all the remedies for their diseases, together with their deceptions, so that he could heal with the plants of the earth.

And Noah wrote in a book everything we taught him concerning every kind of remedy. And the evil spirits were prevented from pursuing Noah’s children. 14 And he gave all the books he had written to Shem, his eldest son, because he loved him more than all his other children.
And Noah slept with his ancestors and was buried on Mount Lubar in the land of Ararat.
He completed nine hundred and fifty years of life: nineteen jubilees and two weeks of years.
Who lived longer on the earth than any other human being, except Enoch, because of his righteousness, in which he was perfect.

And in the thirty-third jubilee, in the first year of this second week of years, Peleg took a wife named Lomna, the daughter of Shinar. She bore him a son in the fourth year of this week, and he named him Reu, for he said, “Look, human beings have become wicked through an evil plan to build themselves a city and a tower in the land of Shinar.”
For they migrated from the land of Ararat eastward into Shinar. In his days they built the city and the tower, saying, “Let us ascend into heaven by it.”

And they began to build. In the fourth week of years they baked bricks in fire, and the bricks served them as stone. The mortar with which they plastered was bitumen that came out of the sea and from springs of water in the land of Shinar.
They spent forty-three years building it. The bricks were [?], thirteen within it, and one-third of one for its length [?]. Its height reached five thousand four hundred and thirty-three cubits.
And the Lord our God said to us, “Look, they are one people, and they have begun to do this. Now nothing will be beyond them.”
And the Lord came down, and we came down with him to see the city and the tower that human beings had built.
And he confused all the speech of their languages, so that no one understood the speech of another. Then they stopped building the city and the tower.
For this reason the whole land of Shinar was called Babel, because there God confused all the languages of human beings.
And the Lord sent a wind against the tower, and it knocked it down to the ground.
In the fourth week of years, in its first year, at the beginning of the thirty-fourth jubilee, they were scattered from the land of Shinar.
And Ham and his children went into the land that was his possession, which he had received as his allotted portion in the southern land.
And Canaan saw that the land of Lebanon as far as the river of Egypt was very good.
And Ham his father, and Cush and Mizraim his brothers, said to him, “You have settled in a land that is not yours and that did not fall to us by lot. Do not do this.
Do not settle in Shem’s dwelling place.
You are cursed, and you will be cursed above all Noah’s children by the curse that we established by oath before the holy Ruler and before Noah our father.”
But he did not listen to them. He and his children settled in the land of Lebanon, from Hamath to the entrance of Egypt, to this day. 34 For this reason that land was called the land of Canaan.

Japheth and his sons went toward the sea and settled in the land allotted to them. Madai saw the land by the sea, and it did not please him. He asked Elam, Asshur, and Arpachshad, his wife's brothers, for land, and he settled in the land of the Medes, near his wife's brothers, where he remained to this day.
He named his dwelling place and the dwelling place of the descendants of the Medes after Madai, their father.

In the thirty-fifth jubilee, in the third week, in its first year, Reu took a wife named Ara, the daughter of Ur son of Chesed. She bore him a son, and he named him Serug, in the seventh week [?] of this week.

In this jubilee, Noah's descendants began to fight, to take captives, to kill one another's brothers, to shed human blood on the earth, to consume blood, to build fortified cities, walls, and towers, to raise individuals over the people, and to establish the beginnings of kingship.

Ud son of Chesed built the city of Araha of the Chaldeans and named it after himself and his father. 4 They made cast images for themselves, and each person bowed down to the idol he had cast for himself.

Prince Mastema exerted himself to bring about all this. Through the spirits placed under his authority, he instigated every error, sin, and offense, bringing corruption and destruction and shedding blood on the earth.
For this reason Serug was given the name Serug, because everyone had turned to committing every kind of sin.
He grew up and settled in Ur of the Chaldeans, near the father of his wife's mother, and he worshiped idols.

She bore him Nahor in the first year of this week of years. He grew up and settled in Ur, among the Chaldeans of Ur. His father taught him the investigations of the Chaldeans, to practice divination and interpret the signs of heaven.

In the thirty-seventh jubilee, in the sixth week of years, in its first year, he took a wife named Ijaska, the daughter of Nestag of the Chaldeans. 10 She bore him Terah in the seventh year of this week of years.
Prince Mastema sent ravens and other birds to eat the seed sown in the land and to devastate the land.
For this reason he was named Terah.
The years began to [?] because of the birds. They ate all the fruit from the trees, and only with great effort could people save a little of all the produce of the land in their days.
In this thirty-ninth jubilee, in the second week of years, in the first year.
In the seventh year of this week of years, she bore him a son.
The child began to recognize the earth's error: everyone was going astray after carved images and impurity.
He began to pray to the Creator of all things to save him from the error of humankind.
The time came to sow seed in the land.

Clouds of ravens came to eat the seed. Abram ran toward them before they settled on the ground and shouted at them before they settled on the ground to eat the seed. He said, "Do not come down! Go back to the place you came from!" And they turned back. 20 That day he did this to the clouds of ravens seventy times. Not a single raven settled anywhere in the fields where Abram was.
Everyone who was with him throughout the fields watched him shouting, and all the ravens turned back.
That year everyone who sowed came to him, and he went with them until the sowing season ended. They sowed their land.

In the first year of the fifth week of years, Abram taught those who made implements for oxen the craft of woodworking. They made a device above the ground, facing the framework of the plow, so that seed could be placed on it. The seed would descend from it onto the plowshare and be buried in the ground. They no longer feared the ravens. 24 They made such devices above the ground on all the plow frames and sowed. Throughout the land they did as Abram had instructed them, and they no longer feared the birds.
In the sixth week of years, in its [?] year, Abram said to his father Terah, "Father!" He replied, "Here I am, my son."
He said, "What help or benefit do we receive from these idols that you worship and bow down before?
For there is no spirit at all in them. They are mute, and they are a delusion of the heart. Do not worship them."
Worship the God of heaven, who sends down rain.

Why do you worship things that have no spirit in them? They are the work of human hands, and you carry them on your shoulders. You gain no help from them, only great disgrace for those who make them and delusion of heart for those who worship them. Do not worship them. 6 He said to him, “I know this too, my son. What should I do about the people who have ordered me to serve before them? 7 If I tell them the truth, they will kill me, because their souls cling to these things, to worship and praise them.”
He told this to his two brothers, and they became angry with him, so he kept silent.
In the fortieth jubilee, in the second week, in its seventh year, Abram took a wife named Sarai, his father's daughter, and she became his wife.
His brother Haran took a wife in the third year of the third week. She bore him a son in the seventh year of this week, and he named him Lot.
His brother Nahor also took a wife.
In the sixtieth year of Abram's life, which was the fourth week of years.
They got up at night and tried to save their gods from the fire.
Haran hurried to save them, but the fire blazed over him, and he was burned in the fire. He died in Ur of the Chaldeans before his father Terah, and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldeans.
Terah left Ur of the Chaldeans with his children to go to the land of Lebanon and the land of Canaan, and he settled in Haran.

In the fifth year of the sixth week of years, Abram sat at night, at the beginning of the seventh month, observing the stars from evening until dawn to see what the year's rainfall would be like. He sat alone, observing. 17 A thought came into his heart, and he said, “All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and the sun—all are in the Lord's hands.”
If he wishes, he makes it rain morning and evening; and if he wishes, he does not send it down. Everything is in his hands.

He prayed that night and said, “My God, my God, God Most High, you alone are my God. You created everything, and everything came into being and exists through the work of your hands. I have chosen you and your divinity.”
“Save me from the power of the evil spirits who rule over the thoughts of human hearts. Do not let them lead us astray from following you, my God. Establish me and my descendants forever.”

He said, “Should I return to Ur of the Chaldeans, whose people seek me out so that I will return to them? Or should I remain here in this place? Make your servant carry out the path that is right before you, and do not let him walk in the error of my heart, my God.”
And when he had finished speaking and praying,
“I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be blessed on the earth.”
“I will be God to you, to your son, to your son's son, and to all your descendants. Do not be afraid. From now on, throughout all the generations of the earth, I am your God.”

The Lord God said to me, “Open his mouth and his ears so that he may hear and speak with his tongue in the revealed language, for it has ceased from the mouths of all humanity since the day of the collapse.” 26 I opened his mouth, his ears, and his lips, and began speaking with him in Hebrew, the language of creation.
He took the books of his ancestors, which were written in Hebrew, and read them. From then on he began to study them, and I explained to him everything he did not understand.
In the seventh year of the sixth week of years, he spoke with his father and told him that he would leave Haran to go to the land of Canaan, see it, and return to him.
His father Terah said to him, “Go in peace. May the eternal God make your path straight, and may the Lord be with you and protect you from every evil.”

“If you find a land pleasing to your eyes to live in, come and take me to you. Take Lot, the son of your brother Haran, with you as your son. May the Lord be with you. 31 But leave your brother Nahor with me until you return in peace, and we will all go together with you.”
Abram left Haran and took Sarai his wife.
He looked, and the land was very pleasant, from the entrance of Hamath as far as the tall oak.
The Lord said to him, “I will give this land to you and your descendants.” 4 He built an altar there and offered incense on it to the Lord, who had appeared to him.
He moved on from there to the hill, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east, and pitched his tent there.

He looked, and the land was broad and very good. Everything grew on it: vines, figs, pomegranates, holm oaks, oaks, terebinths, olive trees, cedars, cypresses, frankincense trees, and all the trees of the countryside. There was water on the mountains.
He blessed the Lord, who had brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and brought him to this hill.
In the first year of the seventh week of years, at the beginning of the first month, he built an altar on this hill and called upon the name of the Lord: “You are my God, the eternal God.”
He offered a burnt offering to the Lord on the altar, so that he would be with him and not abandon him all the days of his life.
He moved on from there and went south until he reached Hebron. Hebron had been built by that time. He stayed there for two years and went into the southern land until Lot came.
Abram went to Egypt in the third year of the week of years and lived in Egypt for five years before his wife was taken away.
Tanis in Egypt was built at that time, seven years after Hebron.
When Pharaoh took Sarai, Abram's wife, the Lord struck Pharaoh and his household with a great plague because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
Abram was very wealthy in possessions: sheep, cattle, donkeys, horses, camels, male slaves, female slaves, and abundant silver and gold.

Pharaoh returned Sarai, Abram's wife, and sent him out of the land of Egypt. He went to the place where he had first pitched his tent, to the site of the altar, with Ai to the east and Bethel to the west. He blessed the Lord his God, who had brought him back in peace.

In this forty-first jubilee, in the third year of the first seven-year period, he returned to this place, burned incense there, and called on the name of the Lord, the Most High God: “My God forever and ever.”
In the fourth year of this seven-year period, Lot separated from him and settled in Sodom. The people of Sodom were exceedingly sinful.
He was grieved in his heart because his brother’s son had separated from him, for he had no children. 19 In that year, when Lot was taken captive.
For I will give all the land you see to you and to your descendants forever.
Get up and walk through its length and breadth, and see it all, for I will give it to your descendants.
In this year Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, and Tidal king of the nations came. They killed the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Sodom fled.
They took Sodom, Admah, and Zeboiim captive. They also took captive Lot, the son of Abram’s brother, with all his possessions, and he went as far as Dan.
Someone who had escaped came and told Abram that his brother’s son had been taken captive.
He mustered those born in his household. [?] Abram went and killed Chedorlaomer, then returned, set aside a tenth of everything, and gave it to Melchizedek.

This law has no limit of time, for he established it for everlasting generations: they are to give the Lord a tenth of everything—from grain, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep. 27 He gave it to his priests to eat and drink joyfully in his presence.
The king of Sodom came to him, bowed before him, and said, “Our lord Abram, give us the people you rescued, but let the spoils be yours.”
Abram said to him, “I raise my hands to God Most High: I will not take anything that belongs to you, from a thread to a sandal strap, so that you cannot say, ‘I made Abram rich.’”

After these events, in the fourth year of this seven-year period, at the beginning of the third month, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a dream, saying, “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your protector, and your reward will be exceedingly great.”

He said, “Lord, Lord, what will you give me, when I go on without children? The son of Maseq, my maidservant—Eliezer of Damascus—will inherit from me. You have given me no offspring. Give me offspring.”
2 He said to him, “This man will not inherit from you. Rather, the one who comes from your own body will inherit from you.”

He brought him outside and said to him, “Look at the sky and count the stars, if you can count them.” 5 He looked at the sky and saw the stars, and he said to him, “So will your descendants be.” 6 He believed the Lord, and it was counted to him as righteousness.

He said to him, “I am the Lord who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you the land of the Canaanites as an everlasting possession, and to be God to you and to your descendants after you.” 8 He said, “Lord, Lord, how will I know that I will inherit it?”
He said to him, “Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a pigeon.”
He took all these in the middle of the month. He was living by the oak of Mamre, which is near Hebron.

He built an altar there, slaughtered all these, and poured their blood onto the altar. He cut them in half down the middle and placed the halves opposite one another, facing each other. But he did not cut the birds apart.
Birds came down upon the pieces, but Abram drove them away and did not let the birds touch them.

At sunset a stupor fell upon Abram, and a great, terrifying darkness fell upon him. Abram was told, “Know for certain that your descendants will be foreigners in a strange land. They will enslave them and afflict them for four hundred years.
“I will also judge the nation that they serve.
“But you will go to your ancestors in peace and be buried at a good old age.
“In the fourth generation they will return here, for the sin of the Amorites has not yet reached its full measure.”
He awoke from sleep and got up. The sun had set, and there was a flame. A smoking furnace and a flame of fire passed between the pieces.

On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your descendants I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates: the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites, Perizzites, Rephaim, Phakorites, and Hivites.”
And he passed on and ascended.
On that night we made a covenant with Abram, like the covenant we made with Noah in this month.
Abram rejoiced and told his wife Sarai all this.
Sarai advised her husband Abram and said to him, “Go in to Hagar, my Egyptian servant, so that perhaps I may build up descendants for you through her.”
Abram listened to his wife Sarai and said to her, “Do it.”
He went in to her, and she conceived and bore a son.
In the fifth year of the fourth week of this jubilee, in the third month, halfway through the month, Abram celebrated the festival of the first harvest of the wheat he had sown.
He offered a new offering on the altar, the first of the grain, to the Lord.
The Lord appeared to him, and the Lord said to Abram, “I am God Almighty. Be pleasing before me and be blameless.
I will establish my covenant between me and you and increase you greatly.”
Abram fell on his face, and God spoke to him, saying,
“Look, my covenant is with you, and I will make you the father of many nations.
Your name will no longer be called Abram. From now on and forever your name will be Abraham, because I have appointed you the father of many nations.
I will make you very great.

I will establish my covenant between me and you and your descendants after you, throughout their generations, as an everlasting covenant, so that I may be your God and the God of your descendants after you. 10 [I will give to you and to your descendants after you] the land where you have lived as a foreigner, the land of Canaan, which you will possess forever, and I will be their God.”

God said to Abraham, “As for you, keep my covenant, you and your descendants after you. Be circumcised, every male among you. Circumcise your foreskins, and this will be the sign of my everlasting covenant between me and you. 12 You shall circumcise every male child among you at eight days old, throughout your generations, including those born in your household.
Anyone born in your household must be circumcised, and those you have bought with gold must be circumcised.
Any uncircumcised male whose foreskin has not been circumcised on the eighth day—that person shall be cut off from his people, because he has broken my covenant.”
The Lord said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, you shall no longer call her Sarai, for her name is Sarah.”
“I will bless her and give you a son through her. I will bless him, and he will become a nation, and kings of nations will come from him.”
Abraham fell on his face and rejoiced, saying in his heart, “Can a son be born to a man who is a hundred years old? And can Sarah, who is ninety years old, give birth?”
Abraham said to God, “If only Ishmael might live before you!”
God said, “Yes.”
“As for Ishmael, I have heard you. Look, I will bless him, make him grow, and multiply him greatly.
But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year.”
When he had finished speaking with him, God went up from above Abraham.

Abraham did as God had told him. He took his son Ishmael, everyone born in his household, and everyone he had bought with money—all the males in his household—and circumcised the flesh of their foreskins.

On that very day Abraham was circumcised, [those born in his household], the members of his household, and all those he had bought with money, including those born to foreigners, were circumcised with him.
This is a law for every generation forever, and there is no circumcision of days.
Everyone who is born whose flesh is not circumcised by the eighth day does not belong to the children of the ordinance that God established with Abraham, but belongs to the children of destruction.
For all the angels of the presence.
You too must command the children of Israel to keep the sign of this covenant throughout their generations as an everlasting ordinance, so that they will not be uprooted from the earth.
For the command was established as a covenant, so that they would keep it forever.

For God did not bring Ishmael, his children, his brothers, or Esau near to himself, nor did he choose them because they were Abraham’s descendants, for he knew them. But he chose Israel to be his people. 31 He made him holy and gathered him out from all humanity.
But over Israel he gave no angel or spirit authority.

Now I tell you that the children of Israel will prove false to this ordinance and will not circumcise their children according to this entire law. They will leave some of the flesh of their circumcision when circumcising their children, and all the children of Beliar will leave their children uncircumcised, just as they were born.

Great wrath from God will come upon the children of Israel because they abandoned his covenant, turned away from his word, mocked and reviled it, and did not carry out the ordinance concerning this sign.
On the first day of the fourth month we appeared to Abraham by the oak of Mamre and spoke with him. We told him that a son would be given to him by Sarah his wife.
Sarah laughed because she heard us speaking these words with Abraham.
We told her the name of her son, Isaac, as it was ordained and written on the heavenly tablets.
When we returned to her at the appointed time, she had conceived a son.
In this month God carried out judgment on Sodom, Gomorrah, Zeboiim, and all the regions of the Jordan. He burned them with fire and sulfur and destroyed them to this day.
Likewise, the Lord will bring judgment upon places [?] where they act as Sodom did, according to the judgment upon Sodom.
We rescued Lot because God remembered Abraham and brought him out from the midst of the overthrow.

He and his daughters committed a sin on the earth such as had not occurred on the earth from the days of Adam until then: a man slept with his daughter. 9 And it was commanded and decreed concerning all his descendants on the heavenly tablets that he would remove them, uproot them, and execute judgment on them like the judgment of Sodom, and that he would leave him no descendants on the earth among humanity on the day of judgment.

In this month Abraham moved from Hebron and went and settled between Kadesh and Shur, in the mountains of Gerar. 11 In the middle of the fifth month he moved from there and settled by the Well of the Oath.

In the middle of the sixth month God visited Sarah and did for her as he had said. 13 She conceived and gave birth to a son in the third month, in the middle of the month, at the time God had told Abraham. Isaac was born at the festival of the first harvest. 14 Abraham circumcised him when he was eight days old. He was the first to be circumcised according to the covenant established forever.

In the sixth year of the fourth week of years we came to Abraham by the Well of the Oath and appeared to him, as we had told Sarah that we would return to her when she had conceived a son. 16 We returned in the seventh month and found Sarah pregnant before us. We blessed her and told her everything that had been decreed for him: that he would not yet die until he had fathered six sons and seen them before he died.
All the descendants of his sons will become nations and will be counted among the nations.

For he will belong to the portion of the Most High, and all his descendants have come under God’s rule, to be the Lord’s own people out of all peoples, and to be a kingdom, a priesthood, and a holy nation.
We went on our way, and we told Sarah everything we had told him. Both of them rejoiced very greatly.
He built an altar there to the Lord, who had made him prosper and who made him rejoice in the land where he lived as a foreigner.

He built shelters for himself and his servants for this festival. He was the first to celebrate the Festival of Shelters on earth. 22 Throughout these seven days, he offered each day on the altar, as a burnt offering to the Lord, two bulls, two rams, seven sheep, and one young goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for himself and his descendants. 23 As peace offerings, he offered seven rams, seven young goats, seven sheep, and seven male goats, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings. He burned all their fat on the altar.
Morning and evening he burned frankincense, galbanum, stacte, nard, myrrh, spice, and costus—all seven of these. He offered them all mixed together in equal portions, as a pure mixture.
He celebrated this festival for seven days, rejoicing with all his heart and all his soul, he and everyone in his household. There was no stranger with him, nor anyone who was uncircumcised.

He blessed his Creator, who had created him in his generation, for he had created him according to his good pleasure. For he knew and was certain that from him would come a righteous plant for everlasting generations, and from him a holy offspring, to be like the one who made everything.
He blessed and rejoiced, and called this festival the Festival of the Lord, a joy acceptable to God Most High.

We blessed him forever, and all his descendants after him throughout all the generations of the earth, because he celebrated this festival at its appointed time, according to the testimony of the heavenly tablets.

For this reason it was ordained on the heavenly tablets concerning Israel that they should celebrate the Festival of Booths with joy for seven days in the seventh month, as something acceptable before the Lord—an eternal law throughout their generations, every year.

There is no limit of days for this, for it is ordained forever for Israel that they should celebrate it and live in booths, place wreaths on their heads, and take leafy branches and willows from the stream.
Abraham took palm shoots and fruit from good trees. Each day he went around the altar with the branches seven times a day. In the morning he praised and glorified his God for everything, with joy.
In the first year of the fifth week of this jubilee, Isaac was weaned. Abraham held a great feast in the third month, on the day his son Isaac was weaned.

And Ishmael, the son of Hagar the Egyptian woman, [?] before his father Abraham in that place. Abraham rejoiced and blessed the Lord because he had seen offspring of his own and had not died without children. 3 And he remembered the words that he had spoken on the day when Lot separated from him.
Sarah saw Ishmael playing and dancing, and Abraham rejoicing with great joy, and she became jealous of Ishmael.
The matter distressed Abraham because of his slave woman and his son, since he was to send them away from him.
The Lord said to Abraham, “Do not be distressed about the boy and the slave woman. Listen to everything Sarah tells you and do it, for through Isaac a name and descendants will be reckoned to you.
As for the son of this slave woman, I will make him into a great nation, because he is your offspring.”

Abraham rose early in the morning, took bread and a skin of water, gave them to Hagar and the boy to carry, and sent her away. 9 She went and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba. The water in the skin ran out, and the boy became thirsty, could no longer walk, and fell down.
His mother picked him up, carried him away, and laid him under an olive tree. She went and sat opposite him, about a bowshot away, for she said, “Let me not see my child die.” She sat there and wept.
An angel of God, one of the holy ones, said to her, “Why are you weeping, Hagar? Get up, pick up the boy, and hold him by the hand, for the Lord has heard your voice and has seen the boy.”
She opened her eyes and saw a well of water. She went and filled her skin with water and gave her boy a drink.

The boy grew up and became an archer, and the Lord was with him. His mother obtained a wife for him from among the daughters of Egypt. 14 She bore him a son, and he called his name Nebaioth, for she said, “The Lord was near to me when I called upon him.”
In the seventh week, in the first year, in the first month of this jubilee, on the twelfth day of the month, there were words in heaven concerning Abraham.
Prince Mastema came and said before God, “Look, Abraham loves his son Isaac and delights in him more than in anything else.”

The Lord knew that Abraham was faithful through every hardship of which he had spoken to him, for he had tested him concerning his land and through famine, and had tested him concerning the wealth of kings.
In everything through which he tested him, he was found faithful. His spirit did not become impatient, and he was not slow to act, for he was faithful and loved the Lord.

The Lord said to him, “Abraham, Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.” 2 He said to him, “Take your son, your beloved whom you love, Isaac, and go to the high country. Offer him on one of the mountains that I will show you.” 3 He rose early in the morning, loaded his donkey, and took with him two of his servants and his son Isaac. He cut the wood for the sacrifice and went to the place on the third day.
He reached a well of water and said to his servants, “Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go, and after we have worshiped, we will return to you.”
He took the wood for the sacrifice and gave it to his son Isaac to carry, while he took the fire and the knife in his hand.
Isaac said to his father, “Father!”
He said, “God will provide for himself a sheep for the burnt offering, my son.”
He built an altar and placed wood on it. He bound his son Isaac and laid him on the wood above the altar. He stretched out his hand to take the knife to slaughter his son Isaac.
I stood before him and before Prince Mastema. The Lord said, “Tell him not to lower his hand against the boy or do anything to him, for I know that he fears God.”
I called to him from heaven and said to him, “Abraham!” He was startled and said, “Here I am.”

I said to him, “Do not stretch out your hand against the boy or do anything to him, for now I know that you fear God and have not withheld your firstborn son from me.” 12 Prince Mastema was put to shame. Abraham raised his eyes and looked, and there was a ram caught and coming forward by its horns [?]. Abraham went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
Abraham called that place “The Lord Has Seen,” as it is said, “The Lord has seen.” It is Mount Zion.

The Lord called Abraham by name a second time from heaven, as he had caused us to appear to speak to him in the name of the Lord. 15 He said, “By myself I have sworn, says the Lord, because you have done this and have not withheld from me your firstborn son, whom you love.”
“All the nations of the earth will be blessed through your descendants because you have obeyed my voice.”
Abraham went to his servants, and they got up and went together to Beersheba.
He celebrated this festival every year for seven days with joy. He called it the Festival of the Lord, corresponding to the seven days during which he went and returned in peace.
Thus it is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets concerning Israel and his descendants: they are to celebrate this festival for seven days with festive rejoicing.
In the first year of the first week of years in the forty-second jubilee, Abraham returned and lived opposite Hebron, which is Kiriath-arba, for two weeks of years.
In the first year of the third week of years in this jubilee, the days of Sarah’s life came to an end, and she died in Hebron.
Abraham went to weep for her and bury her.
For with a patient spirit he spoke with the descendants of Heth, asking them to give him a place in which to bury her body.
The Lord gave him favor before everyone who saw him.
They pleaded with him, saying, “We will give it to you for nothing.” But he would not accept it from them for nothing, for he paid the full price of the place in silver.
All the days of Sarah’s life were one hundred and twenty-seven years. These are two jubilees, four weeks of years, and one year. These were the days of the years of Sarah’s life.

This was the tenth trial with which Abraham was tested, and he was found faithful and patient in spirit. 9 He said nothing concerning the promise about the land that the Lord had said he would give to him and to his descendants after him.

In its fourth year, he obtained a wife for his son Isaac. Her name was Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel, son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, and sister of Laban. Bethuel fathered the Bethuelites and was the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother.

Abraham took a third wife for himself, named Keturah, from among those born in his household, after Hagar had died before Sarah. 12 She bore him six sons—Zimran, Jokshan, Midian, Medan, Ishbak, and Shuah—during two weeks of years.
