In the second year of the sixth week of years, Rebekah bore Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. Jacob was blameless and upright, but Esau was a fierce man, a man of the fields, and hairy. Jacob lived in tents. 14 The boys grew up, and Jacob learned to read, but Esau did not learn, for he was a man of the fields and a hunter. He learned warfare, and all his deeds were fierce.
Abraham loved Jacob, but Isaac loved Esau.
Abraham saw Esau’s deeds and knew that his name and descendants would be reckoned through Jacob.

He said to her, “My daughter, watch over my son Jacob, for he will take my place on earth and be a blessing among humankind and a source of pride for all the descendants of Shem. 18 For I know that the Lord will choose him for himself as a people set apart from all those on the face of the earth.”
“Look, my son Isaac loves Esau more than Jacob, but I see that you rightly love Jacob. 20 Continue to treat him well, and let your eyes rest lovingly upon him.”
“May your hands be strong, and may your heart rejoice in your son Jacob.”

“If anyone can count the sand of the earth, then his descendants too can be counted. 23 May all the blessings with which the Lord blessed me and my descendants belong to Jacob and his descendants for all time. 24 Through his descendants may my name and the names of my ancestors—Shem, Noah, Enoch, Mahalalel, Enosh, Seth, and Adam—be blessed. 25 May they serve to establish heaven, to strengthen the earth, and to renew all the lights above the firmament.”

He called Jacob before the eyes of Rebekah his mother, kissed him, blessed him, and said: 27 “My son Jacob, my beloved, whom my soul loves, may God bless you from above the firmament and give you all the blessings with which he blessed Adam, Enoch, Noah, and Shem, and everything that he spoke of to me.
May the spirits of Mastema not rule over you or your descendants, turning you away from following the Lord, who is your God from now and forever.
May the Lord God be a father to you, and may you be his firstborn son and a people for all time.”
The two of them went out together from Abraham’s presence. 31 Rebekah loved Jacob with all her heart and all her spirit, much more than Esau, but Isaac loved Esau more than Jacob.

In the forty-second jubilee, in the first year of the seventh week, Abraham summoned Ishmael and his twelve sons, Isaac and his two sons, and the six sons of Keturah and their children. 2 He commanded them to keep the way of the Lord, to practice righteousness, each to love his neighbor, and to act likewise in every conflict, so that they would proceed as one against them [?], and to practice justice and righteousness on the earth. 3 They were to raise their children within the covenant that he had made with them and not turn to the right or the left from any of the ways that the Lord commanded us. We were to guard ourselves against all sexual immorality and uncleanness and remove all uncleanness and sexual immorality from among us.

“If any woman among you, even a daughter, commits sexual immorality, burn her with fire. They must not commit sexual immorality by following their eyes and their hearts, taking wives for themselves from the daughters of Canaan, for he will uproot Canaan’s descendants from the earth.”

He told them about the judgment of the Watchers and the judgment of Sodom: how they were judged because of their wickedness, because of sexual immorality, uncleanness, and corruption among themselves. They died because of sexual immorality.

“You too must guard yourselves against all sexual immorality and uncleanness and against every defilement of sin, so that you do not make our name a curse, your whole lives an object of gloating, and all your children subject to destruction by the sword. Otherwise you will become accursed like Sodom, and all who remain of you will be like the children of Gomorrah.
I testify to you, my children: love the God of heaven and hold fast to all his commandments. Do not follow their idols or their uncleanness.
Do not make cast gods or carved images for yourselves, for they are worthless.

Instead, worship the Most High God, bow down to him continually, and seek his presence at all times. Practice righteousness and uprightness before him, so that he may favor you, grant you his mercy, and send down morning and evening rain for you.
It will be a blessing upon the earth, and all the nations of the earth will favor you.”

He gave gifts to Ishmael and his children and to the children of Keturah, and sent them away from his son Isaac. He gave everything to his son Isaac. 12 Ishmael and his children, and the children of Keturah and their children, went together and settled from Paran [?] to the entrance of Babylon, throughout all the land to the east, facing the wilderness.
They mingled with one another, and they were called Arabs and Ishmaelites.

In the sixth year of the seventh week of this jubilee, Abraham summoned his son Isaac and instructed him, saying: “I have grown old, and I do not know the day of my death, for I have reached the fullness of my days.

Look, I am one hundred and seventy-five years old. Throughout all the days of my life I have remembered the Lord and sought with all my heart to do what he desires and to walk uprightly in all his ways. 3 My soul has hated idols, so that I might take care to do the will of the one who created me. 4 For he is the living God, and he is holy, faithful, and righteous above all. With him there is no favoritism or acceptance of bribes, for he is a righteous God, and he executes judgment on all who transgress his commandment and reject his covenant.

And you, my son, keep his commandments, his ordinances, and his judgments. Do not follow the unclean, carved idols, or cast idols. 6 Do not eat any blood of wild animals, livestock, or any bird that flies in the sky. 7 If you slaughter a sacrifice as an acceptable peace offering, slaughter it and pour its blood onto the altar. Offer up all the fat of the sacrifice on the altar, together with fine flour and a grain offering mixed with oil. Offer it all together with its drink offering on the altar, as an offering with a pleasing fragrance before the Lord. 8 Place the fat of the peace offering on the fire on the altar: the fat over the belly, all the fat over the internal organs, the two kidneys and all the fat over them and over the loins, and the liver together with the kidneys. 9 Offer all this up as an acceptable, pleasing fragrance before the Lord, together with its grain offering and its drink offering, as a pleasing fragrance, the food of an offering to the Lord.

Eat its meat on that day and on the next day. Do not let the sun set on it on the second day before it is eaten, and do not let any remain until the third day, for it will not be accepted, because it is not approved, and it must no longer be [?].
Put salt in all your offerings, and do not let the covenant of salt be absent from any of your offerings before the Lord.

Be careful about the wood for the offering, so that you do not bring onto the altar wood such as cypress, laurel, almond, fir, pine, cedar, juniper, [?], olive, myrtle, laurel, the cedar called Arbat, and balsam. 13 From these woods place wood beneath the offering on the altar, after examining its appearance. Do not put down any split wood. Choose solid wood, sound and without any defect, whole and newly grown. Do not put down old wood, because its fragrance has departed and it no longer has the fragrance it had before. 14 Apart from these woods, do not put down any other.
“Keep this commandment and carry it out, my son, so that you may act rightly in everything you do.”

At all times be clean in your body, and wash with water before you go to offer anything on the altar. Wash your hands and feet before you approach the altar. When you have finished making the offering, go back and wash your hands and feet. 17 Let no blood be seen on you or on your clothes. Be careful, my son, about blood; be very careful. Cover it with earth. 18 Do not eat blood, for blood is life. Do not eat any blood.

Do not show favoritism in any matter involving human blood, so that it is not shed through you without judgment. For blood that is shed brings guilt upon the earth, and blood cannot be cleansed of human blood [?] except by the blood of the one who shed it.
Do not accept favoritism or a gift in a matter involving human blood. Blood for blood, and it will be acceptable before God Most High.
I see, my son, that all the deeds of humankind are sinful and evil, and all their works are unclean, contemptible, and repulsive.
“Be careful not to follow their ways or walk in their footsteps, and do not commit a sin leading to death before God Most High.”
Keep away from all their deeds and all their uncleanness. Keep the commands of God Most High, do his will, and be upright in everything.

He will bless you in all your deeds and raise up from you a plant of righteousness throughout the earth, through all the generations of the earth. My name and your name will never fall silent beneath heaven, for all time.

Go in peace, my son. May God Most High, my God and your God, strengthen you to do his will. May he bless all your offspring, the remainder of your offspring, for everlasting generations, with every blessing of righteousness, so that you may be a blessing throughout the earth.
And he left him rejoicing.

In the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee, in the second year, the year in which Abraham died, Isaac and Ishmael came from the Well of the Oath to their father Abraham to celebrate the Feast of Weeks, the feast of the first harvest. Abraham rejoiced because both his sons had come. 2 Isaac had many possessions in Beersheba, and Isaac would go and inspect his possessions and return to his father. 3 In those days Ishmael came to see his father, and they all came together. Isaac slaughtered a sacrificial offering and offered it up on his father's altar, which he had made in Hebron.
He offered a peace offering and held a joyful feast in the presence of his brother Ishmael.
Isaac himself sent a pleasing peace offering by the hand of Jacob, for Abraham to eat and drink.
He ate and drank and blessed God Most High, who created heaven and earth, who made all the abundance of the earth and gave it to human beings to eat and drink and to bless their Creator.

“And now I praise you, my God, because you have let me see this day. Look, I am one hundred and seventy-five years old, an old man full of days, and all my days have been peaceful. 8 The sword of an enemy has not overcome me.

May your [?] and your peace rest upon your servant and upon the offspring of his children, so that they may be your chosen people and inheritance from among all the nations of the earth, from now through all the days of the earth’s generations, for all ages.”

He called Jacob and said to him, “My son Jacob, may the God of all bless you and strengthen you to practice righteousness and do his will before him. May he choose you and your offspring to be a people for his inheritance, according to his will, for all time.”
He came near and kissed him.

“Be strong before other people, and as you [?] among all the offspring of Seth, may your ways and the ways of your children be righteous, so that you may become a holy people. 13 May God Most High give you all the blessings with which he blessed me and with which he blessed Noah and Adam. May they rest upon the crown of the head of your holy offspring, throughout every generation and forever.
May he cleanse you from every filthy impurity, so that you may be forgiven for all the guilt of the errors you committed unknowingly.
May he renew his covenant with you, so that you may be a people for his inheritance throughout all ages.
And you, my son Jacob, remember my words and keep the commandments of Abraham your father.
They offer their sacrifices to senseless things and bow down to demons.
They have no understanding with which to think, and their eyes do not see.

“And you, my son Jacob, may God Most High help you, and may the God of heaven bless you and keep you away from their impurity and all their wrongdoing. 20 Be careful, my son Jacob, not to take a wife from any of the descendants of the daughters of Canaan.”

For through Ham’s sin Canaan went astray, and all his offspring will be wiped from the earth, along with all who remain of him. None of them will escape on the day of judgment. 22 All who worship idols, and those who are hated, have no hope at all in the land of the living, for they will descend into Sheol and go to the place of judgment.
Do not fear, my son Jacob, and do not be terrified, son of Abraham. May God Most High protect you from destruction and rescue you from every path of error.

This house I built for myself, to place my name upon it on the earth. It has been given to you and your offspring forever, and it will be called the house of Abraham. It has been given to you and your offspring forever, for you will build my house and establish my name before God forever. Your offspring and your name will endure throughout all the generations of the earth.”

He finished instructing and blessing him. 26 They both lay down together on one bed, and Jacob slept in the embrace of Abraham, his grandfather. He kissed him seven times, and his affection and his heart rejoiced over him. 27 He blessed him with all his heart and said, “God Most High, God of all and Creator of all, who brought me out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give me this land to possess forever, and so that I might establish holy offspring who would be blessed forever—

bless Jacob my son, in whom I rejoice with all my heart and affection. May your kindness and mercy remain upon him and his offspring for all time. 29 Do not abandon him or neglect him, from now through all eternity.
Bless him with all your blessings, from now through all the days of eternity.”
He placed Jacob’s two fingers upon his eyes and blessed the God of gods. He covered his face, stretched out his feet, and slept the eternal sleep.
Throughout all this, Jacob lay in his embrace and did not know that Abraham his grandfather had died.
Jacob awoke from his sleep.
He rose from his embrace, ran, and told Rebekah his mother.
Isaac fell upon his father’s face, wept, and kissed him.
A cry was heard in Abraham’s house.
His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the double cave beside Sarah his wife.

He lived for three jubilees and four weeks of years, a hundred and seventy-five years, and completed the days of his life, old and full of years. 9 For the lifetimes of the earliest people were nineteen jubilees.
For Abraham was perfect in all his actions before God.
And every generation that arises from now until the day of the great judgment will grow old quickly, before completing two jubilees.

In those days, if a man lives for a jubilee and a half, they will say of him, “He has lived a long time.” Most of his days will be pain, toil, and distress, and there will be no peace. 13 For there will be plague upon plague, wound upon wound, distress upon distress, bad news upon bad news, illness upon illness, and every similar evil punishment, one along with another: illness, upheaval, snow, hail, frost, fever, chills, numbness, famine, death, the sword, and captivity.
And all this will come upon the evil generation that corrupts the earth with the filth of sexual immorality, with uncleanness, and with the abominations of their deeds.
Then they will say of the people of earlier times, “Their days were long, as much as a thousand years, and good.”
And in that generation the children will rebuke their fathers and their elders because of sin, injustice, the words of their mouths, and the great evils they commit.
For they have all acted wickedly, and every mouth speaks wrongdoing.

Look, the earth will be destroyed because of all their deeds. There will be no grain or wine, and no oil, because all their deeds are faithless. They will all perish together—wild animals, livestock, and birds.

They will fight one another: the young against the old, and the old against the young; the poor against the rich; the lowly against the great; and the needy against the ruler, over the law and the covenant. For they have forgotten the commandment, the covenant, the festival, the new moon, the Sabbath, the jubilee, and every judgment.

They will rise up with swords and slaughter to bring them back to the way, but they will not return until they have shed much blood on the earth, fighting one another. 21 Those who survive will not turn from their wickedness to the way of righteousness, for they will all rise up for deceit and wealth, so that each may take everything belonging to his neighbor. They will call themselves by a great name, but not in truth or righteousness, and they will defile the holy of holies with the impurity of their corrupt abominations.
A great plague from the Lord will come upon the deeds of that generation, and he will hand them over to the sword, judgment, captivity, plunder, and destruction.

And he will stir up against them the sinners of the nations, who have neither mercy nor compassion for them and show favor to no one, neither the old nor the young nor anyone else. For they are wicked and powerful, more wicked than all other human beings. They will commit violence in Israel and wrongdoing against Jacob. They will shed much blood on the earth, and there will be no one to gather the dead and no one to bury them.

In those days they will cry out, call out, and pray to be saved from the hands of the sinful nations, but there will be no one to save them. 25 The heads of the children will turn white with gray hair, and a child twenty-one years old will look as old as someone a hundred years old. Their bodies will waste away through misery and suffering.
And in those days the children will begin to seek out the laws, to seek the commandment, and to return to the path of righteousness.

And their days will begin to increase and grow longer, generation after generation among humanity, and day after day, until their lifespans approach a thousand years, and their years become more numerous than their days had been. 28 There will be no old person and no one whose days are full, for they will all be infants and children. 29 They will complete all their days in peace and joy, and they will live. There will be no Satan and no evil one to destroy them, for all their days will be days of blessing and healing.
Then God will heal his servants. They will rise and see great peace, and he will drive out his enemies. The righteous will see, give thanks, and rejoice with joy forever and ever.
Their bones will rest in the earth.
“And you, Moses, write down these words, for this is how they are written, and they will be entered as testimony on the heavenly tablets for the generations forever.”

After Abraham died, the Lord blessed his son Isaac. He left Hebron and went to live by the Well of the Vision for seven years, beginning in the first year of the third week of this jubilee. 2 In the year of the fourth week, a famine began in the land, apart from the earlier famine that had occurred in Abraham’s days.
Jacob cooked a lentil stew, and Esau came from the field hungry. He said to his brother Jacob, “Give me some of this wheat stew.”
Esau said to himself, “I am going to die. What use is being the firstborn?” He said to Jacob, “I give it to you.”
And Jacob said to him, “Swear to me today.” And he swore to him.

And Jacob gave his brother Esau bread and stew, and he ate until he was satisfied. Esau despised his birthright. For this reason his name was called Esau and Edom, because of the wheat stew that Jacob gave him in exchange for his birthright.
And Jacob grew in greatness, while Esau sank from his greatness.
There was a famine in the land, and Isaac set out to go down to Egypt in the second year of this week. He went to Abimelech, king of the Philistines, at Gerar.
And God appeared to him and said to him, “Do not go down to Egypt. Stay in the land that I tell you about. Live as a foreigner in that land, and I will be with you and bless you.
For I will give all this land to you and your descendants, and I will fulfill the oath that I swore to your father Abraham. I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars of heaven.
And all the nations of the earth will be blessed through your descendants, because your father obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my laws, my ordinances, and my covenant.”

And he lived in Gerar for twenty-one years. 13 Abimelech gave orders concerning him and everything that belonged to him, saying, “Anyone who touches him or anything that belongs to him must be put to death.”
And Isaac grew great among the Philistines. He had many possessions: cattle, sheep, camels, donkeys, and much property. 15 And they sowed in the land of the Philistines.
And all the wells that Abraham’s servants had dug during Abraham’s lifetime, the Philistines destroyed after Abraham died and filled with earth.
And Abimelech said to Isaac, “Go away from us, for you have become much greater than we are.”
And they went back and dug the wells of water that the servants of his father Abraham had dug.
Isaac’s servants dug wells in the valley and found flowing water. The shepherds of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s shepherds, saying, “This water is ours.”

They dug another well, and they quarreled over that one too, so he named it Narrowness. He moved away, and they dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. He named it Room, and Isaac said, “Now the Lord has made room for us, and we have increased in the land.”

He went up from there to Beersheba in the first year of the first week of years in the forty-fourth jubilee. 22 The Lord appeared to him that night, at the beginning of the first month, and said to him, “I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and greatly multiply your descendants like the sand of the earth, for the sake of Abraham my servant.”
He built there the original altar that Abraham his father had built.
They dug a well and found flowing water. 25 Isaac’s servants also dug another well, but they found no water.

He called that place the Well of the Oath, because there he swore an oath to Abimelech, to Ahuzzath his deputy, and to Phicol, commander of his guard. 27 Isaac realized that day that he had sworn to make peace with them under compulsion.
On that day Isaac cursed the Philistines and said, “May the Philistines be cursed among all the nations for the day of wrath and anger.”

Those who escape the sword of the enemy and the Kittim will be uprooted from under heaven by a righteous people in judgment, because they will be enemies and foes of my children throughout their days on earth. 30 No remnant will be left to them, nor anyone who escapes on the day of wrath and judgment.

“For even if he ascends to heaven, he will be brought down from there. Even if he establishes himself firmly in the earth, he will be torn out from there. Even if he hides among the nations, he will be uprooted from there. And even if he descends into Sheol, his punishment will increase there.”
Even if he goes into captivity, those who seek his life will kill him along the way, and neither a name nor descendants will be left to him anywhere on earth.
Thus it is written and engraved concerning him on the heavenly tablets, to be done to him on the day of judgment, so that he may be uprooted from the earth.

In the second year of this week of years, in this jubilee, Rebekah called Jacob her son and spoke to him, saying, “My son, do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan, as Esau your brother did. He took two wives from the descendants of Canaan, and they have embittered my soul by all their impure deeds, for all their deeds are sexual immorality and lust. There is no righteousness at all among them, for they are evil. 2 But I love you very deeply, my son, and my heart and my affection bless you at every hour of the day and every watch of the night.

“Now, my son, listen to my words and do what your mother wishes. Do not take a wife from the daughters of this land, outside my father’s household and my father’s family. Take a wife from my father’s household, and may God Most High bless you. May your offspring be righteous offspring, and your descendants holy.”

Then Jacob spoke with Rebekah his mother and said to her, “Look, Mother, I am now nine weeks of years old. I have known no woman, nor have I touched one or become betrothed. Nor do I intend to take a wife for myself from any of the descendants of the daughters of Canaan. 5 For I remember, Mother, the words of Abraham our father, and what he commanded me: not to take a wife from any of the descendants of the house of Canaan, but to take a wife for myself from the descendants of my father’s house and from my relatives. 6 I heard some time ago, Mother, that daughters had been born to Laban your brother, and I have set my heart on taking a wife from among them.”

“For this reason I have guarded myself in spirit, so that I might not sin or corrupt myself in any of my ways throughout my life. For our father Abraham gave me many commands concerning marriage and sexual immorality, along with everything else he commanded me. 8 For these twenty-two years my brother has argued with me, repeatedly saying to me, ‘My brother, take as your wife a sister of my two wives.’ But I am unwilling to do as he has done.”

“I swear before you, Mother, that throughout my life I will not take a wife for myself from any of the descendants of the daughters of Canaan, nor will I act wickedly as my brother has done. 10 Do not be afraid, Mother. Be assured that I will do your will, walk uprightly, and never corrupt my ways.”

Then she lifted her face toward heaven, spread out the fingers of her hands, opened her mouth, and blessed the Most High God, who created heaven and earth. She gave him thanks and praise. 12 She said, “Blessed be the Lord God, and blessed be his name forever and ever.”

“Bless him, Lord, and place a righteous blessing in my mouth, so that I may bless him.” 14 At that moment a spirit of righteousness descended into her mouth. She placed both her hands on Jacob’s head and said:

“Blessed are you, O righteous Lord, their God forever. May he bless you above every generation of humanity, grant you, my son, the path of righteousness, and reveal righteousness to your descendants. 16 May he multiply your children during your lifetime, and may they equal the months of the year in number. May their children multiply and become more numerous than the stars of heaven, and may their number exceed the sand of the sea. 17 May he give them this desirable land, as he said he would give it to Abraham and to his descendants after him for all time, and may they possess it as an everlasting possession. 18 May I see blessed children born to you during my lifetime, my son, and blessed descendants. May all your descendants be holy.

“Just as you have given rest to your mother’s spirit during her [?], may the womb of the woman who bore you and my compassion likewise bless you. May my breasts bless you, and may my mouth and tongue praise you. Multiply, 20 grow great, and spread throughout the earth. May your descendants be complete throughout all the world, amid the joy of heaven and earth.”
“May your name and your descendants endure forever.
“Blessed be whoever blesses you, and cursed be everyone who falsely curses you.”
She kissed him and said to him, “May the Lord of eternity love you, just as your mother’s heart and affection rejoice in you, and may he bless you.” Then she stopped blessing him.

“Now take your hunting equipment, your sling and your bow, and go out into the countryside. Hunt for me and catch something for me, my son. Prepare for me the food I love and bring it to me, so that I may eat and bless you before I die.”
Rebekah was listening as Isaac spoke to Esau.
Esau went into the wilderness to hunt, to catch something and bring it to his father.

Rebekah called Jacob her son and said to him, “Look, I heard Isaac your father speaking with Esau your brother, saying, ‘Hunt something for me, prepare food for me, and bring it to me, so that I may eat and bless you before the Lord before I die.’

“Now, my son, listen to what I command you. Go to your pasture and fetch me two good young goats. I will prepare them as food for your father, just as he likes. You will bring it to your father, and he will eat, so that he may bless you before the Lord before he dies.”
Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, “Mother, I will not withhold anything that my father would eat and enjoy. But I am afraid, Mother, that he may recognize my voice and want to feel me.”

You know that I am smooth-skinned and that my brother Esau is hairy. In his eyes I will seem like someone deceiving him, and I will be doing something he did not command me to do. He will become angry with me, and I will bring a curse on myself instead of a blessing.
His mother Rebekah said to him, “Let your curse fall on me, my son. Only listen to me.”
Jacob listened to his mother Rebekah.
Rebekah took the favorite clothes of her older son Esau, which she had with her in her house, and dressed her younger son Jacob in them.
She placed the cooked food and the bread she had prepared into the hands of her son Jacob.
He went in to his father and said, “I am your son. I have done as you told me. Get up, sit down, and eat some of what I have hunted, Father, so that your soul may bless me.”
Isaac said to his son, “How have you found it so quickly, my son?”
Jacob said, “Your God brought it before me.”
Isaac said to him, “Come near, my son, so that I may feel you and determine whether you are my son Esau or not.”

Jacob approached his father Isaac, and Isaac felt him and said, 18 “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are Esau’s hands.” He did not recognize him, for this was a change brought about from heaven to alter his spirit. Isaac did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like Esau’s hands, so that he would bless him.

He said, “Are you my son Esau?” He answered, “I am your son.” Then he said, “Bring it to me, and let me eat some of what you have hunted, my son, so that my soul may bless.” 20 He brought it to him, and he ate. [?] wine for him, and he drank.
His father Isaac said to him, “Come close and kiss me, my son.”
He smelled the scent and fragrance of his clothes, blessed him, and said, “Look, the scent of my son is like the scent of a field that the Lord has blessed.”
“May the Lord give to you and increase your share of the dew of heaven and the dew of the earth. May he multiply abundant wheat and oil for you.”

“Be lord over your brothers, and may your mother’s children bow down to you. May all the blessings with which the Lord blessed me and blessed Abraham my father belong to you and your descendants forever. Cursed be whoever curses you, and blessed be whoever blesses you.”
After Isaac finished blessing his son Jacob, and Jacob had just gone out from Isaac his father, he hid himself.
He too prepared food and brought it to his father.
Isaac his father said to him, “Who are you?” He said to him, “I am Esau, your firstborn, your son. I have done as you commanded me.”

Isaac was extremely astonished and said, “Who was it who went out, hunted game for me, and brought it? I ate some of everything before you came, and I blessed him. May he be blessed, together with all his descendants, forever.”
When Esau heard the words of his father Isaac, he cried out very loudly and bitterly and said to his father, “Bless me too, Father!”
He said to him, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessings.”
He said, “Have you not kept a blessing for me, Father?”
Esau said to his father Isaac, “Do you have only one blessing, Father? Bless me too, Father!” And Esau raised his voice and wept.
“You will live by your sword, and you will serve your brother.”
Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him. He said to himself, “The days of mourning for my father will soon arrive, and then I will kill my brother Jacob.”
“Look, your brother Esau is planning revenge against you and intends to kill you.”

“Now, my son, listen to me. Get up and flee to my brother Laban in Haran. Stay with him for a few days, until your brother’s anger subsides, he lets go of his anger against you, and he forgets everything you did to him. Then I will send for you and bring you back from there.”
Jacob said, “Let him not be afraid. If he wants to kill me, I will kill him.” 5 She said to him, “I must not lose both my sons in one day.”

Jacob said to his mother Rebekah, “Look, you know that my father has grown old, and I see that his eyes have grown dim. If I leave him, it will seem wrong to him that I am abandoning him and going away from you.”
Rebekah said to Jacob, “I will go in and tell him, and he will send you away.”
Rebekah went in and said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of the two daughters of Heth whom Esau has taken as his wives.”

Isaac called his son Jacob, blessed him, and instructed him, saying, 10 “Do not take a wife from any of the daughters of Canaan. Get up and go to Mesopotamia, to the house of Bethuel, your mother’s father. Take a wife there from among the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.”

“May God Almighty bless you, make you great, and multiply you, so that you become a community of peoples. May he give you and your descendants after you the blessings he gave my father Abraham, so that you may inherit the land where you have lived as a foreigner, and all the land that the Lord gave Abraham. Go in peace, my son.”
Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Mesopotamia, to Laban, the son of Bethuel the Syrian and the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s mother.
After Jacob set out for Mesopotamia, Rebekah grieved for her son and wept.
Isaac said to Rebekah, “My sister, do not weep for my son, for he will go in peace and return in peace. 15 May God Most High protect him from every evil and be with him.”
“For I know for certain that his ways will prosper wherever he goes, until he returns to us in peace and we see him safe and sound.”
Do not be afraid for him, my sister, for he is upright in his ways. He is a blameless man and faithful, and he will not be abandoned. Do not weep.
Isaac comforted Rebekah about her son Jacob, and he blessed him.

Jacob left Beersheba to go to Haran in the first year of the second week of the forty-fourth jubilee. He reached Luz, which is in the mountains and is Bethel, on the first day of the first month of this week. He reached the place in the evening and turned aside from the road, to the west of the highway, that night. He slept there because the sun had set.
He took one of the stones of that place and put it under that tree. He was traveling alone.
He dreamed that night, and there was a ladder set up on the earth, with its top reaching into heaven.
He spoke with Jacob and said, “I am the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land on which you are sleeping I will give to you and to your descendants after you.
Your descendants will be like the sand of the earth, and you will increase toward the west and the east, the north and the south.
[?] I will be with you and protect you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land in peace. For I will not leave you until I have done everything I have told you.”

Jacob slept a sleep and said, “Truly, this place is the house of the Lord, and I did not know it.” He was afraid and said, “How awe-inspiring this place is! It is nothing other than the house of the Lord, and this is the gate of heaven.”

Jacob rose early in the morning, took the stone he had placed at his head, and set it up as a pillar for a sign. He poured oil on its top and named that place Bethel, though previously the town had been named Luz.

Jacob prayed a prayer to the Lord, saying, “If the Lord is with me and protects me on this journey I am making, and gives me bread to eat and clothing to wear, and I return to my father’s house in peace, then the Lord will be my God.”
In the first year of the third week, he said to him, “Give me my wife, for whom I have served you seven years.” Laban said to Jacob, “I will give you your wife.”
Laban held a wedding feast. He took Leah, his older daughter, and gave her to Jacob as his wife. He gave her his slave woman Zilpah as a servant. Jacob did not know, for Jacob thought she was Rachel.
He slept with her, and there she was—Leah.
Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, for Leah’s eyes were weak, though she was very beautiful in appearance. Rachel had beautiful eyes and a beautiful appearance, and she was very lovely.
Laban said to Jacob, “It is not customary in our land to give the younger before the older.”
You too must command the children of Israel.

Laban said to Jacob, “Let the seven days of this woman’s wedding feast pass, and I will give you Rachel, on condition that you serve me another seven years, tending my sheep as you did during the first week.”
When the seven days of Leah’s wedding feast had passed, Laban gave Rachel to Jacob, on condition that he serve him another seven years. He gave her Bilhah, Zilpah’s sister, as a servant.
He served another seven years for Rachel, because Leah had been given to him for nothing.
The Lord opened Leah’s womb, and she conceived and bore Jacob a son. He named him Reuben.
Rachel’s womb was closed, because the Lord saw that Leah was hated, while Rachel was loved.
Jacob again slept with Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a second son. He named him Simeon.
Jacob again went in to Leah, and she conceived and bore him a third son. He named him Levi.
He again slept with her, and she bore a fourth son.
Through all this, Rachel was jealous of Leah because she herself bore no children.
When Rachel saw that Leah had borne Jacob four sons—Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah—
He went in to her, and she conceived and bore him a son.
Jacob again went in to Bilhah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a second son. Rachel named him Naphtali, on the fifth day of the seventh month, in the second year of the fourth week of years.

When Leah saw that she had become barren and was no longer bearing children, she too became jealous of Rachel. She too gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife. She conceived and bore a son, and Leah named him Gad, on the twelfth day of the eighth month, in the third year of the fourth week of years.
He again went in to her, and she conceived and bore him a second son. Leah named him Asher, on the second day of the eleventh month, in the fifth year of the fourth week of years.
Jacob went in to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a son. He named him Issachar, on the fourth day of the fifth month, in the fourth year of the fourth week of years.
Jacob went in to her a second time, and she conceived and bore two children, a son and a daughter. She named the son Zebulun and the daughter Dinah.
God had mercy on Rachel and opened her womb.

In the days when Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wives and my children, so that I may go to my father Isaac and establish a household for myself. For I have completed the years during which I served you in exchange for your two daughters, and I will go to my father’s house.”
Laban said to Jacob, “Stay with me for wages, and tend my flocks for me again, and take your wages.”
They agreed between themselves that he would give him as his wages every sheep born among the lambs and goats that had dark markings and was spotted with white.

All the sheep gave birth to spotted young, all bearing speckled markings, and to dark, speckled young. The sheep again gave birth to young resembling themselves. Everything with markings belonged to Jacob, and everything without markings belonged to Laban.
Jacob’s livestock increased greatly, and he acquired cattle, sheep, donkeys, camels, male servants, and female servants.
Laban and his sons became jealous of Jacob. Laban took his sheep back from him and watched him with evil intent.
Jacob saw that Laban was going to shear his sheep.
For he told them how he had seen everything in a dream, and everything that had been said to him, that he should return to his father’s house.
Jacob blessed the God of his father Isaac and the God of Abraham, his father’s father.

In the seventh year of the fourth week of years, Jacob turned toward Gilead in the first month, on the twentieth and [?] day. Laban pursued him and overtook Jacob on Mount Gilead in the third month, on the thirteenth day.
God did not allow him to act harshly toward Jacob, for he appeared to him in a dream at night. Laban told Jacob about it.

On the fifteenth day of that month, Jacob held a feast for Laban and everyone who had come with him. On that day Jacob swore an oath to Laban, and Laban to Jacob, that neither would cross Mount Gilead to harm the other.
He held a celebration there as a witness. Therefore that place was named Celebration of Witness, after this celebration.
Formerly they called the land of Gilead the land of Raphael, for it was the land of the Rephaim.
Their dwelling places extended from the land of the Ammonites to Mount Hermon, and their royal cities were Karnaim, Ashtaroth, Edrei, Misor, and Beon.
God destroyed them because of their evil deeds, for they were extremely wicked.
Jacob sent Laban away, and he went to Mesopotamia, the land of the east.
He crossed the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the tenth and [?] day.

In the first year of the fifth week of years in this jubilee, he crossed the Jordan and settled beyond the Jordan. He pastured his sheep from the Sea of the Heap as far as Beth-shan, as far as Dothan, and as far as [?] Akrabbim.
From all his possessions he would send his father Isaac clothing and food, meat and drink, milk and butter, milk cakes, and dates from the lowlands.

He also sent these to his mother Rebekah four times a year, at the intervals of the months: between plowing and harvesting, between spring and the rainy season, and between winter and summer, at Abraham’s dwelling.
For Isaac had returned from the Well of the Oath and gone up to the dwelling of his father Abraham. He lived there, away from his son Esau.
For when Jacob went to Mesopotamia, Esau took Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, as his wife. He gathered all his father’s flocks and his wives, went up, and settled on Mount Seir.
Isaac went up from Beersheba and settled at the dwelling place of his father Abraham, in the hill country of Hebron.
From there Jacob would send his father and mother everything he sent them, from time to time, for all their needs.
1. After Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Laban went to shear his sheep, for they were far away from him, a three-day journey.
There they abducted Dinah, Jacob’s daughter, into the house of Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, the ruler of the land. He slept with her and defiled her.
He begged her father to give her to him as a wife, and he also asked her brothers for her as his wife.

Simeon and Levi entered Shechem unexpectedly and carried out judgment on all the men of Shechem. They killed every man they found in it and did not leave even one alive. They killed them all cruelly because they had defiled Dinah, their sister.

So from now on nothing like this shall be done to defile a daughter of Israel. For judgment was decreed against them in heaven, that all the men of Shechem should be destroyed by the sword, because they had committed a disgraceful act in Israel. 6 God delivered them into the hands of Jacob’s sons, so that they would destroy them with the sword and execute judgment upon them.

If any man in Israel wishes to give his daughter or his sister to any man descended from the nations, he must certainly die, and they shall stone him with stones, because he has committed a disgraceful act in Israel.
Let no sexual immorality or uncleanness be found in Israel throughout all the days of the generations of the earth, for Israel is holy to the Lord.
For this is what has been decreed and written on the heavenly tablets concerning all the descendants of Israel: whoever defiles them must certainly die, and they shall stone him with stones.

There is no time limit for this law, no pardon, and no forgiveness whatsoever. Rather, the man who has defiled his daughter shall be destroyed from among all Israel, because he has given some of his offspring to Moloch and has sinned by defiling them.

And you, Moses, command the Israelites and testify to them that they must not give any of their daughters to the nations or take wives from among the daughters of the nations, for this is detestable before the Lord.

For this reason I have written for you in the words of the law everything that the people of Shechem did to Dinah, and how Jacob’s sons spoke, saying, “We will not give our daughter to a man who has a foreskin, for that is a disgrace to us.” 13 It is a disgrace to Israel for those who give their daughters or take wives from among the daughters of the nations, for this is unclean and detestable in Israel.
Israel cannot be purified of this uncleanness when a man has a wife from among the daughters of the nations.
For it is punishment upon punishment and curse upon curse, and every judgment, punishment, and curse will come.
There shall be no favoritism, no partiality toward anyone, and no acceptance from his hands of produce, offerings, burnt offerings, fat, or a pleasing fragrance, so as to accept him.
For this reason I commanded you, saying, “Bear this witness against Israel.”
The descendants of Levi were chosen for the priesthood and as Levites, to serve before the Lord as we do at all times.
In this way they will record blessing and righteousness for him as a testimony on the heavenly tablets, before the God of all.

We remember the righteousness that a person practiced during his lifetime, at every season of the year. They will record it for a thousand generations, and it will come to him and to his descendants after him. He will be recorded as a friend and a righteous person on the heavenly tablets.

I have written all these things for you and commanded you to tell the children of Israel not to commit sin, transgress the ordinance, or break the covenant established for them to observe, so that they may be recorded as friends. 22 But if they transgress and follow any of the ways of uncleanness, they will be recorded on the heavenly tablets as enemies. They will be erased from the book of the living and recorded in the book of those who perish, among those who are uprooted from the earth.

On the day when Jacob's sons killed the people of Shechem, a written record was brought up to heaven for them, stating that they had acted righteously and justly and taken vengeance on sinners. It was recorded as a blessing.

They brought their sister Dinah out of Shechem’s house and took as plunder everything in Shechem: their sheep, cattle, donkeys, all their possessions, and all their flocks. They brought everything to their father Jacob.
He spoke to them about their slaughter of the city, because he was afraid of the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites and Perizzites.
The terror of God came upon all the cities around Shechem, and they did not rise up to pursue Jacob’s sons, because dread had fallen upon them.
1. In the first year of the sixth week, he went up in peace to Salem, east of [?], in the fourth month.

At the new moon, Jacob said to everyone in his household, “Purify yourselves and change your clothes. Let us get up and go to Bethel, where I prayed to him on the day when I fled from my brother Esau. He has been with me and has brought me back to this land in peace. Remove the foreign gods that are among you.”

They handed over the foreign gods and the things in their ears and around their necks. Rachel also gave Jacob all the idols she had stolen from her father Laban. He burned them, broke them to pieces, destroyed them, and hid them beneath the oak in the land of Shechem.
He went up to Bethel at the new moon of the seventh month. He built an altar in the place where he had slept and set up a pillar there.
Isaac said, “Let my son Jacob come, so that I may see him before I die.”
Jacob went to his father Isaac and his mother Rebekah, to the house of his father Abraham. He took two of his sons with him, Levi and Judah, and came to his father Isaac and his mother Rebekah.
Rebekah came out of the tower to the tower’s gate to kiss Jacob and embrace him.
She saw his two sons.
Jacob went to his father Isaac, into his room where he lay.
The dimness passed from Isaac’s eyes, and he saw Jacob’s two sons, Levi and Judah.
He told him that they were indeed his sons: “You have truly seen that they are indeed my sons.”
They approached him, and he turned and kissed them and embraced them all together.
The spirit of prophecy descended into his mouth, and he took Levi with his right hand and Judah with his left hand.
He turned to Levi first and began by blessing him. He said to him, “May the Lord of all, the Lord of all ages, bless you.

May God give you and your descendants great and glorious exaltation. May he bring you and your descendants near to himself, above all flesh, to serve in his sanctuary like the angels of the Presence and like the holy ones.
They shall be judges, princes, and messengers for all the descendants of Jacob’s sons. They shall speak the word of God in righteousness and pronounce all his judgments in righteousness.
Your mother named you Levi, and she named you truly. You shall be joined to the Lord and be a partner with all Jacob’s sons.
All who hate you shall fall before you, and all your enemies shall be uprooted and perish. Whoever blesses you shall be blessed, and all the people who curse you shall be cursed.”

To Judah he said, “May God give you strength and might to trample all who hate you. May you and one of your descendants be rulers over Jacob’s sons. May your name and the name of your descendants go forth and spread throughout all the earth and its cities.
Through you may help come to Jacob, and through you may Israel’s salvation be found.
On the day when you sit on the throne of your righteous glory, there shall be great peace for all the descendants of the beloved one’s sons.”
He turned and kissed him again and embraced him. He rejoiced greatly because he had seen the children of Jacob, his righteous son.
He came out from between his feet, fell down, and bowed to him, and he blessed them.
He placed Jacob’s two sons, one at his right and one at his left, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
During the night Jacob told his father everything about the great kindness God had shown him.
Isaac blessed the God of his father Abraham, who had not withheld his mercy and righteousness from the son of his servant Isaac.

In the morning Jacob told his father Isaac about the vow he had made to the Lord, the vision he had seen, and how he had built an altar and prepared everything needed to offer a sacrifice before the Lord in accordance with his vow. He also told him how he had come to carry him there on a donkey.
Isaac said to his son Jacob, “I cannot come with you, because I have grown old and cannot endure the journey. Go in peace, my son, for I am 165 years old.
I know, my son, that you have come for my sake.
Make your preparations and fulfill the vow you made. Do not delay fulfilling your vow, for the vow will be required of you.”
He said to Rebekah, “Go with your son Jacob.” Rebekah went with her son Jacob, and Deborah went with her, and they arrived at Bethel.
Jacob remembered the prayer with which his father had blessed him and his two sons, Levi and Judah. He rejoiced and blessed the God of his fathers Abraham and Isaac.

He said, “Now I know that I and my children have an everlasting hope before the God of all.” Thus it was ordained concerning both of them, and they will record it for them as an everlasting testimony on the heavenly tablets, just as Isaac blessed them.
He spent that night in Bethel. Levi dreamed that they had appointed and established him and his descendants as priests of God Most High forever.
Jacob rose early in the morning on the fourteenth day of this month.
In those days Rachel conceived her son Benjamin, and Jacob counted his sons beginning with him.

On the [?] and fifth day of this month, he brought to the altar fourteen bulls from the cattle, twenty-eight rams, forty-nine sheep, sixty lambs, and twenty-nine young goats, as a burnt offering on the altar and an acceptable offering, a pleasing fragrance before God.
This was his offering in fulfillment of the vow he had made to give a tenth, together with their sacrifices and their drink offerings.
When the fire consumed it, he burned frankincense above it on the fire.
He, all his sons, and his people ate joyfully there for seven days, blessing and thanking the Lord, who had delivered him from all his troubles and granted what he had prayed for.
He took a tenth of all the clean animals and offered them as a burnt offering. He gave the unclean animals to his son Levi, and he gave him all the human beings.
Levi served as priest at Bethel before his father Jacob, in preference to his ten brothers, and he was priest there.
For this reason a law is prescribed on the heavenly tablets: a second tithe is to be taken and eaten before the Lord, year after year, in the place where he has chosen to make his name dwell.
This is the written ordinance to be observed year after year: the second tithe is to be eaten before the Lord in the place he has chosen.
For grain is to be eaten in its year, until the time of the year's grain harvest; wine until the time of the grape harvest; and oil until the time of its season.
Anything left over from it that grows old shall be considered defiled. It shall be burned in fire, because it has become unclean.
Likewise, they shall eat it together in the sanctuary and shall not let it grow old.
The entire tithe of cattle and sheep shall be holy to the Lord and shall belong to his priests, who shall eat it before him year after year.

On the following night, on the twenty-second day of this month, Jacob planned to build up that place, enclose a courtyard, and consecrate it, making it a sanctuary forever for himself and his descendants after him.
The Lord appeared to him at night, blessed him, and said to him, “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob alone; they shall call your name Israel.

He said to him again, “I am the Lord who created heaven and earth. I will make you grow and multiply you exceedingly. Kings will come from you, and they will rule everywhere that human footsteps tread.”

I will give your descendants all the land beneath heaven, and they shall rule among all the nations as they wish. After this they shall gather the whole earth together and possess it forever.” 20 He finished speaking with him and ascended from him, and Jacob watched until he ascended into heaven.

He saw in a vision at night, and there was an angel descending from heaven with seven tablets in his hands. He gave them to Jacob, and Jacob read them. He read everything written in them that would happen to him and his children throughout all ages.
He showed him everything written on the tablets and said to him, “Do not build up this place or make it an everlasting sanctuary, and do not settle here, for this is not the place.”
For you will die peacefully in Egypt, and in this land you will be buried with honor in the tomb of your fathers, with Abraham and Isaac.
Do not be afraid, for everything will happen just as you have seen and read. You too must write down everything just as you have seen and read it.
Jacob said, “Lord, how will I remember everything that I have read and seen?”
He ascended from him.

He stayed there one more day and offered sacrifices on it corresponding to all that he had offered on the previous days. He called it “Addition,” because that day had been added, and he called the previous days a festival.
In this way he indicated that it should be so, and it is written on the heavenly tablets.
It was named Addition, because it is what they add [?] to the days of the festival, according to the number of days in the year.

On the night of the twenty-third day of this month, Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died. They buried her below the city, beneath the oak by the river. He called that place Deborah's River, and its oak the Oak of Deborah's Mourning.
And Rebekah went and returned to the house, to his father Isaac.
He followed his mother until he approached the land of Kabratan, and he stayed there.
And Rachel gave birth to a son at night, and she named him Son of My Sorrow, because she suffered while giving birth to him. But his father named him Benjamin.
And Rachel died there and was buried in the land of Ephrathah, which is Bethlehem.
And Jacob went and camped south of Migdal Eder [?]. He and Leah his wife went to his father Isaac on the first day of the tenth month.

And Reuben saw Bilhah, Rachel’s maidservant and his father’s concubine, bathing in water, and secretly desired her. 3 And he hid at night and entered Bilhah’s house at night. He found her lying alone in her bed, asleep in her house. 4 And he lay with her. She woke and saw that Reuben was lying with her in the bed.
And she was ashamed before him and removed her hands from him, and he fled.
And she lamented this matter greatly, but she did not speak of it, not to anyone.

And when Jacob came and sought her out, she said to him, “I am not pure for you, because I have been defiled in relation to you. Reuben defiled me and lay with me at night while I was asleep. I did not know until he lifted my skirt and lay with me.”
Jacob was very angry with Reuben because he had slept with Bilhah, for he had uncovered his father's nakedness.
And Jacob no longer approached her, because Reuben had defiled her. And anyone who uncovers his father’s nakedness—his deed is very wicked, and he is rejected before the Lord.

For this reason it is written and ordained on the heavenly tablets that a man must not lie with his father’s wife or uncover his father’s nakedness, because it is unclean. The man who lies with his father’s wife and the woman must both be put to death, because this deed is unclean on the earth.
And there must be no uncleanness before our God among the people whom he chose as his own possession.

And again it is written a second time: “Cursed be anyone who lies with his father’s wife, because he has uncovered his father’s nakedness.” And all the Lord’s holy ones shall say, “So be it! So be it!”

And you, Moses, command the children of Israel to observe this command, for it carries a sentence of death and is an impurity. There is no forgiveness or atonement forever for a man who does this, except to put him to death, kill him, stone him with stones, and uproot him from among the people of our God.
For anyone who does this in Israel must not remain alive on the earth for even one day, because he is rejected and unclean.

And they must not say, “Reuben was allowed to live and was forgiven after he lay with his father’s concubine-wife, and she too was forgiven, although she had a husband and her husband Jacob, his father, was alive.”
For until that time the ordinance, judgment, and law had not been fully revealed to everyone.
And this law has no end, nor is there any forgiveness for this, except that both must be removed from among the people. They must be killed on the day they do it.

And you, Moses, write this down for Israel, so that they may observe it and not do anything like this or stray into a sin punishable by death. For the Lord our God is a judge who shows no favoritism and accepts no bribes.
And tell them this ordinance, so that they may listen, take care, and guard themselves against these things, and not be destroyed or removed from the earth.
And there is no greater sin than the sexual immorality they commit on the earth, because Israel is a people holy to the Lord their God.
And in the third year of the sixth week, Jacob and all his children traveled and settled in Abraham’s house, near his father Isaac and his mother Rebekah.
And these are the names of Jacob’s children: Reuben, his firstborn.
And they went and bowed down before Isaac and Rebekah.
And in the sixth year of this week of years, in the forty-fourth jubilee.
And all seven kings of the Amorites gathered against them to kill them, hiding beneath the trees, and to plunder their livestock.

And Jacob, Levi, Judah, and Joseph were in the house with Isaac their father, for his spirit was sorrowful, and they could not leave him. Benjamin was the youngest, and for this reason he stayed with him.

And the kings of Tappuah, the kings of Aresa, the kings of Seragan, the kings of Shiloh, the king of Gaash, the king of Beth-horon, and the king of Maannisakir came, along with all those who lived in these hills, who lived in the wooded land of Canaan.
And they reported to Jacob, saying, “Look, the kings of the Amorites have surrounded your sons, and their herds have been plundered.”

And he arose from his house, he and his three sons and all his father’s sons and his own sons. He went against them with six thousand men carrying swords. 7 And he killed them in the pasture of Shechem. They pursued those who fled and killed them with the sword.
And he gathered his herds together.
And he returned in peace.
And in the seventh year of this week of years, he sent Joseph.
And they deceived him and plotted against him to kill him.
And Jacob’s sons slaughtered a male goat, dipped Joseph’s garment in its blood, and sent it to their father Jacob on the tenth day of the seventh month.

And he mourned that entire night, because they brought it to him in the evening. He mourned his death bitterly and said that a wild beast had eaten Joseph. And everyone in his household mourned with him that day, and they continued grieving and mourning with him throughout that entire day.
And his sons and his daughter rose to comfort him, but he would not be comforted over his son.

And on that day Bilhah heard that Joseph had perished, and she died while mourning him. She had been living in Qafr​​atef. Dinah his daughter also died after Joseph had perished. These three sorrows came upon Israel in one month. 16 And they buried Bilhah opposite Rachel’s tomb, and they buried Dinah his daughter there also.
And he continued mourning for Joseph for one year and did not stop, for he said, “I will go down to the grave mourning for my son.”

For this reason it was ordained for the children of Israel that they should afflict themselves on the tenth day of the seventh month, the day when the news that made him weep for Joseph reached his father Jacob, so that on that day atonement might be made for him with young goats.
And this day was ordained for them to mourn on it over their sins, all their offenses, and all their errors, so that they might purify themselves on this day once a year.
And after Joseph disappeared, Jacob’s sons took wives for themselves.
And Simeon returned and took another wife from Mesopotamia, like his brothers.

And in the first year of the first week of years in the forty-fifth jubilee, Rebekah called her son Jacob and gave him instructions concerning his father and his brother, that Jacob should honor them all the days of his life.
And Jacob said, “I will do everything as you have commanded me, for this is an honor and a great privilege for me, and it is righteousness for me before the Lord to honor them.
And you, mother, know all my deeds from the day I was born until this day, and everything in my heart, that I always intend good toward everyone.

How could I not do what you have commanded me, to honor my father and my brothers? [?] Tell me, mother, what wrongdoing you have seen in me, and I will turn away from it, and mercy will be shown to me.”
And she said to him, “My son, in all my days I have seen no crooked deed in you, but only uprightness. Yet I tell you the truth, my son: I will die this year, and I will not live beyond this year.”

And Jacob laughed at his mother’s words, because his mother told him that she would die, although she was sitting before him with her strength intact and had lost none of her vigor. For she went in and out and could see, her teeth were strong, and no illness had afflicted her throughout her life.

And Jacob said to her, “I would be blessed, Mother, if my days approached the length of your life and my strength remained with me as yours does. You will not die, for you speak to me about your death in vain and to no purpose.”
And she went to Isaac and said to him, “I ask one request of you: make Esau swear that he will not harm Jacob or pursue him with hatred.
You know everything he has done from the day his brother Jacob went to Haran until this day, how he has abandoned us with all his heart.
And when we plead with him, asking him for what belongs to us, he acts like a man who is doing us a favor.
And he is bitter toward you because you blessed your son Jacob, who is blameless and upright, for there is no evil in him, but only goodness.”
And Isaac said to her, “I too know and see how Jacob acts toward us, that he honors us with all his heart.”
“Even now my heart is troubled over his deeds, and neither he nor his descendants will be saved, for they will be destroyed from the earth and uprooted from under heaven.
Yet you tell me to make him swear that he will not kill his brother Jacob.
But even if he wishes to kill his brother Jacob, he will be handed over into Jacob’s hands and will not escape from his hands, for he will fall into his hands.
And do not be afraid for Jacob, for Jacob’s guardian is greater, mightier, more glorious, and more praiseworthy than Esau’s guardian.

And Rebekah sent and summoned Esau, and he came to her. She said to him, “My son, I have a request to make of you. Say that you will do it, my son.” 19 And he said, “I will do everything you tell me, and I will not refuse your request.”

And she said to him, “I ask you, on the day when I die, to bring me in and bury me near Sarah, your father’s mother, and that you and Jacob love one another. Let neither seek harm against his brother, but love one another, so that you may prosper, my sons, and be honored in the land. Let no enemy rejoice over you, and may you be a blessing and receive mercy in the eyes of all who love you.”
And he said, “I will do everything you tell me, and on the day of your death I will bury you near Sarah, my father’s mother, just as you have desired that her bones should be near your bones.”
“And I love Jacob my brother more than all other flesh, and I have no brother in all the earth except him alone.”
“And I likewise beg you to admonish Jacob concerning me and my children, for I know that he will surely reign over me and over my children.”
And I swear to you that I will love him and that no evil will be sought against him all the days of my life, but only good. [?]
And she summoned Jacob in Esau’s presence and commanded him according to the words she had spoken with Esau.
And he said, “I will do as you wish. Trust me: no evil against Esau will come from me or from my children. I will not be the first to act against him, but will only love him. [?]”
And she and her sons ate and drank that night.

In the sixth year of this week of years, Isaac called both his sons, Esau and Jacob. They came to him, and he said to them, “My children, I am going the way of my fathers, to the eternal home where my fathers are.
Bury me near Abraham my father, in the double cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite, which Abraham purchased as a burial place. Bury me there, in the grave that I dug for myself.
“And this I command you, my sons: practice righteousness and justice on the earth, so that the Lord may bring upon you everything that the Lord said he would do for Abraham and his descendants.”
My children, live together loving your brothers as a man loves himself. Let each man seek what is good for his brother, and act together on the earth. Let them love one another as themselves.
Concerning idols, I warn you to reject them and oppose them, and not to love them, for they are full of deception for those who worship them and bow down to them.

My children, remember the Lord, the God of Abraham your father, whom I too have worshipped and served in righteousness and joy, so that he may multiply you and make your descendants as numerous as the stars of heaven, and plant you in the earth as a righteous planting that will never be uprooted, throughout all generations forever.

And now I bind you by a great oath—for there is no oath greater than this—by the glorious, honored, great, splendid, wonderful, mighty, and great name of the one who made the heavens and the earth and everything together:

Each of you must love his brother with mercy and righteousness, and no one must desire evil for his brother, from now and forever, throughout all the days of your lives, so that you may prosper in all your deeds and not be destroyed.

If any of you seeks evil against his brother, know from now on that everyone who seeks evil against his brother will fall into his brother’s hands. His brother will uproot him from the land of the living, and his descendants will be destroyed from beneath heaven.
On the day of turmoil, curse, wrath, and anger, with consuming fire, just as he burned Sodom, so he will burn that man’s land, his city, and everything that belongs to him.
My children, I tell you and testify against you concerning the judgment that will come upon the man who wishes to do harm to his brother.”
On that day he divided all his possessions between the two of them. He gave the larger portion to the one who had been born first, together with the tower and everything around it.
And he said, “I will give this larger portion to the one who was born first.”
Esau said, “I sold it to Jacob and gave my birthright to Jacob. Let it be given to him. I have nothing at all to say about it, because it belongs to him.”

Isaac said, “May a blessing rest upon you, my children, and upon your descendants this day, because you have put me at ease. My heart is not troubled about the birthright, since you will not cause strife over it. 16 May the Lord Most High bless the man who acts righteously, both him and his descendants forever.”
He finished commanding and blessing them, and they ate and drank together in his presence. He rejoiced because there was harmony between them. They left him and rested that day and slept.
Isaac lay down in his bed that day rejoicing, and he slept the eternal sleep.
Esau went to the land of Edom, to Mount Seir, and lived there.
And Jacob lived in the hills of Hebron, in the tower in the land where his father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.

And Leah his wife died in the fourth year of the second week of years of the forty-fifth jubilee. He buried her in the double cave, near Rebekah his mother, to the left of the tomb of Sarah, his father’s mother. 22 And all her children and his children came to mourn Leah his wife with him and to comfort him concerning her, for he was mourning her. 23 For he had loved her very deeply since Rachel her sister died, because she was blameless and upright in all her ways and honored Jacob.
And he remembered all the deeds she had done during her life, and he mourned her greatly, for he loved her with all his heart and with all his soul.
And on the day when Isaac, the father of Jacob and Esau, died, Esau’s sons heard that Isaac had given the rights of the firstborn to Jacob his younger son.
And they quarreled with their father, saying, “Why, when you are the elder and Jacob is younger, did your father give him the rights of the firstborn and pass you over?”
He said to them, “I sold my birthright to Jacob for a little lentil stew.

And now our father has made both me and him swear that neither of us will seek evil against his brother, that we will live in love and peace with one another, and that we will not corrupt our ways.” 5 They said to him, “We will not listen to you and make peace with him, because our forces are stronger than his, and we are stronger than he is. We will go against him, kill him, and destroy his children. If you do not go with us, we will harm you too.”

Now listen to us. Let us send messengers to Aram, Philistia, Moab, and Ammon, and choose for ourselves picked men who are ready for battle. Let us march against him, fight him, and uproot him from the earth before he gains strength.
Their father said to them, “Do not go and do not wage war against him, or you will fall before him.”
They said to him, “This is just how you have behaved from your youth until this day, putting your neck under his yoke. But we will not listen to this proposal.”
They sent to Aram and to Adoram, their father's friend, and hired a thousand chosen warriors and fighting men to accompany them.
A thousand picked men, hired from Moab and from the Ammonites, came to them.
They said to their father, “Go out and lead them, or we will kill you.”
He was filled with rage and fury when he saw his sons compelling him to go ahead and lead them against his brother Jacob.

Then he remembered all the evil against his brother Jacob that lay hidden in his heart. He did not remember the oath he had sworn to his father and mother, that he would never seek any harm against his brother Jacob throughout his life.
Through all this, Jacob did not know that they were coming against him to fight.

The people of Hebron sent word to him, saying, “Look, your brother has come against you to fight you with four thousand men armed with swords and carrying shields and weapons of war.” They told him because they loved Jacob more than Esau, for Jacob was a more gracious and merciful man than Esau.
Jacob did not believe it until they came close to the fortress. 17 He closed the gates of the fortress.
Then Esau answered him, “Neither human beings nor the wild animals of the earth have a binding oath that they have sworn to keep forever.
You will hate me and my children forever, and there will be no brotherhood between us.

Listen to these words I tell you: If a pig changes its skin and its bristles become like wool [?], and if horns grow on its head like the horns of a stag or a sheep, then I will act as a brother toward you.
And if wolves make peace with lambs so that they do not eat them,
and if a lion becomes a shelter for an ox,
and if ravens become white like a heron, then know that I love you and will make peace with you.”
When Jacob saw that he intended evil against him with all his heart and all his soul, intending to kill him,
he then told his own men and his servants to attack him and all his companions.

Then Judah spoke to his father Jacob and said, “Father, take your bow and shoot your arrow. Strike the enemy and kill the adversary. May you have strength, for we will not kill your brother: he is your kinsman, and in our eyes he is your equal in honor.”
Then Jacob drew his bow, shot an arrow, and struck his brother Esau, bringing him down. 3 He shot another arrow and struck Adoran the Aramean in the left breast, killing him.
Then Jacob’s sons and their servants went out, dividing into groups on the four sides of the fortress.
Judah went out in front, with Naphtali and Gad and fifty men, on the south side of the fortress. They killed everyone they encountered, and not one of them escaped.
Levi, Dan, and Asher went out on the east side of the fortress, with fifty men. They killed their opponents from Moab and Ammon.
Reuben, Issachar, and Zebulun went out on the north side of the fortress, with fifty men. They killed their Philistine opponents.
Simeon, Benjamin, and Enoch the son of Reuben went out on the west side of the fortress, with fifty men. They killed four hundred strong warriors from Edom and the Horites, and six hundred fled.
Jacob’s sons pursued them as far as Mount Seir.
The descendants of Jacob subdued the descendants of Esau on Mount Seir and brought their necks low, so that they became servants of the descendants of Jacob.
They sent to their father to ask whether they should make peace with them or kill them.

Jacob sent word to his sons to make peace. They made peace with them and imposed the yoke of tribute on them, requiring them to pay tribute to Jacob and all his sons. 13 They continued paying tribute to Jacob until the day Jacob went down to Egypt.
The descendants of Edom have not thrown off the yoke of tribute that the twelve sons of Jacob imposed on them, to this day.
These are the kings who reigned in Edom before a king reigned over the descendants of Israel, to this day, in the land of Edom.
Balak son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
Balak died, and Jobab son of Zerah, from Bozrah, reigned in his place.
Jobab died, and Husham, who was from the mountains of Teman, reigned in his place.
Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the territory of Moab, reigned in his place. The name of his city was Avith.
Hadad died, and Samlah, who was from Masrekah, reigned in his place.

Samlah died, and Shaul, who was from Rehoboth on the River, reigned in his place. 22 Shaul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place. 23 Baal-hanan son of Achbor died, and Hadad reigned in his place. His wife's name was Mehetabel, daughter of Matred, daughter of Mezahab.
These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom.
Jacob lived in the land where his father had lived as a foreigner, the land of Canaan. 2 These are the descendants of Jacob.
He appointed Joseph over his entire household.
The Egyptian left everything in Joseph's care, because he saw that the Lord was with him and that the Lord made everything he did prosper.
Joseph was handsome and very pleasing in appearance.
He did not give himself over.

Joseph remembered these words and was unwilling to sleep with her. 8 She pleaded with him for one year and then another, but he refused to listen to her. 9 She pressed him and seized him in the house to force him to sleep with her.
When the woman saw that he would not sleep with her, she accused him before his master, saying, “Your Hebrew servant, whom you love, wanted to force me to sleep with him.”
The Egyptian saw Joseph's garment and the broken door.
He remained there in prison.

He left everything in his care, and the chief prison keeper paid no attention to anything under his charge, because Joseph did everything and the Lord brought it to completion. He stayed there for two years.

At that time Pharaoh, king of Egypt, became angry with his two officials, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker. He put them in prison in the house of the chief cook, in the prison where Joseph was confined.

The chief prison keeper assigned Joseph to attend to them, and he served in his presence. 16 Both of them, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker, dreamed a dream, and they told Joseph. 17 Just as he interpreted it for them, so it happened to them.
The chief cupbearer forgot Joseph in prison, who had made known to him what would happen to him. He did not remember to tell Pharaoh what Joseph had told him, because he forgot.

At that time Pharaoh dreamed two dreams in one night concerning the famine that would come upon the whole land. He awoke from his sleep and summoned all the dream interpreters in Egypt and the magicians. He told them both his dreams, but they could not understand them.
Then the chief cupbearer remembered Joseph and told the king about him. They brought him out of prison, and the king recounted both his dreams before him.
He said in Pharaoh's presence that his two dreams were one.
